item.title: Sheff Wed will move swiftly to find new manager
item.description: [BBC] Dave Challinor left Stockport with a 53.7% win rate [Getty Images] The decision to part with Henrik Pedersen won't have been a knee-jerk reaction. It would be easy to assume it was solely motivated by disappointing defeats at Notts County and Doncaster Rovers, where Sheffield Wednesday were poor. Yet from Wigan to Stockport to Salford in the EFL Trophy, to Huddersfield then the two latest defeats - unconvincing performances were becoming a common theme. A lot of good work has taken place at the club since the end of last season. The hospitality and commercial arm of the club is totally revamped. Key personnel have been appointed to finally give Wednesday an infrastructure. The training ground now has a proper, functioning gym. I have been shown around the new facility and it is a big upgrade. There is a big emphasis from the top on a cultural shift at the club. David Storch is very keen to connect and support the community, as we saw with his recent backing for Sheffield Children's Hospital. James Silverwood, the chair of the Supporters Trust, has also been invited to join the board. We have often said it is like two year's work has taken place in a single summer. With all the change occurring at Hillsborough, the product on the pitch also needed to evolve and develop. I doubt anyone at Wednesday is demanding they romp the league. They had to rebuild the squad under significant EFL restrictions after all. There had to be evidence of progress, though. The playing side of the club had to improve, just as everything else was growing off the pitch. There was no sign of that. Wednesday were a confusing team to watch. There wasn't enough fight and you didn't feel like they were set up to do what it takes to win their tricky October away games. It is one thing to turn it on at home against Bromley and Wimbledon. You have got to find a way to win at Meadow Lane, or Doncaster during a storm, too. My understanding is Wednesday are moving swiftly in the process of appointing a replacement. This will not drag on - but the necessary time will be taken so a proper process can take place. Dave Challinor is the red-hot favourite because of his prior working experience at Stockport with Simon Wilson, Wednesday's sporting director. I would not rush to assume his appointment is a foregone conclusion though. If that were the case, he'd probably just be announced on Monday. There will be other candidates in the running and we'll see who emerges. I am not sure it will be a manager in work given the Owls are limited by EFL spending restrictions. That is a shame because a candidate like Paul Warne at MK Dons would've been ideal. He has won four promotions from League One, five in total, and managed Derby when they had the same EFL limits (and got them up). Supporters contacted us suggesting a host of names on Sunday. David Storch is very keen to connect and support the community, as we saw with his recent backing for Sheffield Children's Hospital. James Silverwood, the chair of the Supporters Trust, has also been invited to join the board. We have often said it is like two year's work has taken place in a single summer. With all the change occurring at Hillsborough, the product on the pitch also needed to evolve and develop. I doubt anyone at Wednesday is demanding they romp the league. They had to rebuild the squad under significant EFL restrictions after all. There had to be evidence of progress, though. The playing side of the club had to improve, just as everything else was growing off the pitch. There was no sign of that. Wednesday were a confusing team to watch. There wasn't enough fight and you didn't feel like they were set up to do what it takes to win their tricky October away games. It is one thing to turn it on at home against Bromley and Wimbledon. You have got to find a way to win at Meadow Lane, or Doncaster during a storm, too. My understanding is Wednesday are moving swiftly in the process of appointing a replacement. This will not drag on - but the necessary time will be taken so a proper process can take place. Dave Challinor is the red-hot favourite because of his prior working experience at Stockport with Simon Wilson, Wednesday's sporting director. I would not rush to assume his appointment is a foregone conclusion though. If that were the case, he'd probably just be announced on Monday. There will be other candidates in the running and we'll see who emerges. I am not sure it will be a manager in work given the Owls are limited by EFL spending restrictions. That is a shame because a candidate like Paul Warne at MK Dons would've been ideal. He has won four promotions from League One, five in total, and managed Derby when they had the same EFL limits (and got them up). Supporters contacted us suggesting a host of names on Sunday. One that came up regularly was Steve Cooper, but I understand that he can be ruled out. The Owls need a winner. Someone adaptable who can make the most of the assembled squad and know how to get a result. In the meantime, Matt Hamshaw will lead the team in interim charge. He is very experienced in League One and a respected coach. He knows the club well having played for Wednesday and would be an asset on the staff for whoever takes over. A simplified approach on Tuesday against Cambridge, a vocal home support and the players stepping up to be counted, as Liam Cooper called for post-Doncaster, can help get Wednesday back on track before the new boss arrives. item.title: The Ralf Rangnick advice Man United ignored as crisis deepens
item.description: The inescapable nature of Manchester United’s latest crisis could be felt as Michael Carrick exited Old Trafford following a humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday. Eight matches without a win and staring at another managerial change just months after Carrick has delivered the feel good factor once again following the turbulent reign of Ruben Amorim. Now braced for 14 years without a Premier League title, following the Sir Alex Ferguson era, 16th and just a point above the relegation zone after eight matches. During Ralf Rangnick’s time as interim manager of United, from 2021-22, the German offered some prescient advice on what it will take to overhaul the club, with Erik ten Hag and Amorim’s doomed spells in charge following over the next four years. “It's crystal clear, it's not that difficult, you don't need glasses to analyse it and see where the problems are,” Rangnick famously stated back in 2022. “So now it's only about how we solve them. It's clear, not enough to do some little, minor amendments, and issues here and there. Some minor cosmetic things. “In medicine, you would see, this is an operation at the open heart. This is also something that not one single person, as a manager, can do. All respect to Jurgen and Pep, I'm sure that they didn't do all the things themselves, there were other people involved. Ralf Rangnick endured a miserable time at Manchester United (PA Archive) “If people want to work together, it makes sense, I still believe, it doesn't take two to three years to change those things. This can happen within one year.” United now face more turbulence, with Eddie Howe among the favourites to succeed Carrick, should the club opt for another change. After already exiting the Carabao Cup, United have a midweek break and a trip to Chelsea in the Premier League on Saturday up next.

item.title: Report Card: Jets Lose To Miami 28-25 In Week 7
item.description: The New York Jets had a chance to gain some ground on the New England Patriots and after their loss on Thursday night to the Chicago Bears . They were at home against the winless Miami Dolphins . It was what many believed to be a perfect recipe for the team to get their third win of the season. Instead, the Jets put together a brutal first half on both sides of the football and lost their second straight, 28-25, to the Dolphins . This was one of those games where the Jets played with zero passion from the beginning and couldn't get a big stop when it mattered most. The Jets are now at 2-5 and Aaron Glenn's seat is officially a raging inferno after giving Miami their first win of the season. Here is Jets Wire's report card for the team's inexcusable loss to Miami: Passing Offense: C+ Geno Smith threw for three touchdowns on the afternoon, including two to Mason Taylor, but is was mostly in the second half when the team was trailing. Omar Cooper Jr. had his second touchdown of the season as well as his second 100 yard receiving game in a row. As we mentioned, Taylor was excellent this afternoon with five catches for 62 yards and those two scores. However, it was another week when Garrett Wilson wasn't featured at all in this offense. GW finished with two catches for 26 yards on three targets. He was also caught on a sideline camera venting his frustrations to Geno Smith. I'm not sure why Frank Reich doesn't get him involved more and this has potential to get very ugly if it continues. And, for all of Reich's excitement when he selected him, he barely uses Kenyon Sadiq as the rookie tight end only had one catch for six yards. Rushing Offense: B Braelon Allen had his second 100 yard game of the season as he finished with 104 yards on 17 carries and added six catches for 30 yards in the passing game. He's really developing into a strong running back for this team and it's fair to wonder what his role will be when Breece Hall returns from his calf injury. Reich must figure out a way to get both of his running backs on the field at the same time. Whether he's capable of that creativity is another story. However, this team's inability to get one measly yard each week when it matters is beyond embarrassing. This time it was in the fourth quarter where the Jets were one yard away from a game tying touchdown and had to settle for a field goal because Andrew Beck and Allen couldn't get one yard. Like I said last week, it must be Reich's arrogance as he insists on running it up the middle each time just to get one yard. Passing Defense: D+ Malik Willis at times today looked like Dan Marino as he finished 14 for 21, 208 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. He led Miami on two consecutive scoring drives to start the game as the Jets were asleep at the wheel on defense. It was another week of no interceptions and no turnovers for a defense that is starting to show cracks in the foundation. Caleb Douglas's only two receptions on the day went for touchd
item.content:encoded: The New York Jets had a chance to gain some ground on the New England Patriots and after their loss on Thursday night to the Chicago Bears . They were at home against the winless Miami Dolphins . It was what many believed to be a perfect recipe for the team to get their third win of the season. Instead, the Jets put together a brutal first half on both sides of the football and lost their second straight, 28-25, to the Dolphins . This was one of those games where the Jets played with zero passion from the beginning and couldn't get a big stop when it mattered most. The Jets are now at 2-5 and Aaron Glenn's seat is officially a raging inferno after giving Miami their first win of the season. Here is Jets Wire's report card for the team's inexcusable loss to Miami: Passing Offense: C+ Geno Smith threw for three touchdowns on the afternoon, including two to Mason Taylor, but is was mostly in the second half when the team was trailing. Omar Cooper Jr. had his second touchdown of the season as well as his second 100 yard receiving game in a row. As we mentioned, Taylor was excellent this afternoon with five catches for 62 yards and those two scores. However, it was another week when Garrett Wilson wasn't featured at all in this offense. GW finished with two catches for 26 yards on three targets. He was also caught on a sideline camera venting his frustrations to Geno Smith. I'm not sure why Frank Reich doesn't get him involved more and this has potential to get very ugly if it continues. And, for all of Reich's excitement when he selected him, he barely uses Kenyon Sadiq as the rookie tight end only had one catch for six yards. Rushing Offense: B Braelon Allen had his second 100 yard game of the season as he finished with 104 yards on 17 carries and added six catches for 30 yards in the passing game. He's really developing into a strong running back for this team and it's fair to wonder what his role will be when Breece Hall returns from his calf injury. Reich must figure out a way to get both of his running backs on the field at the same time. Whether he's capable of that creativity is another story. However, this team's inability to get one measly yard each week when it matters is beyond embarrassing. This time it was in the fourth quarter where the Jets were one yard away from a game tying touchdown and had to settle for a field goal because Andrew Beck and Allen couldn't get one yard. Like I said last week, it must be Reich's arrogance as he insists on running it up the middle each time just to get one yard. Passing Defense: D+ Malik Willis at times today looked like Dan Marino as he finished 14 for 21, 208 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. He led Miami on two consecutive scoring drives to start the game as the Jets were asleep at the wheel on defense. It was another week of no interceptions and no turnovers for a defense that is starting to show cracks in the foundation. Caleb Douglas's only two receptions on the day went for touchdowns, including a 63 yard score that sealed the victory for Miami. Rushing Defense: D Ollie Gordon II had his second 100 yard game on the ground this season as the running back finished with 103 yards and a touchdown. Miami as a team finished with 156 yards on the ground and also got a score from Willis. This unit has badly regressed as they were gashed quite a bit on the afternoon. And when the Jets needed one last stop on defense to get the ball back, but promptly gave up two yards to Willis on a first down that sealed their fate. Special Teams: C Jason Sanders missed his second field goal of the season, this time a 40 yarder that hit the right upright. In a broader sense, that field goal was the difference between the game being tied and the Jets losing by three. However, it's a bit unfair to blame Sanders when the rest of the team decided to take the day off. The Jets decided to use Malik McClain on kick returns today, but it wasn't much better than before. Coaching: F It's becoming par for the course that the Jets have at least one game this year where they don't show up or even worse, play down to their competition. This was that game for this year. The Jets played with no passion and there was no game plan. They took Miami too lightly and they paid the price. Reich had another brutal game as the play caller and now has a major issue on his hands with his star receiver. There is no universe where Garrett Wilson should only have three targets for an entire game, even if you have another receiver like Omar Cooper Jr., who was excellent again today. I cannot defend the indefensible with Aaron Glenn and this team looked unprepared and disinterested. There is no excuse for that whatsoever. You cannot lose to a winless Miami Dolphins team at home. That is a fireable offense especially with so much at stake this season. No one would blame Woody Johnson if he fired Glenn tomorrow, but we most likely will have to stomach this until the end of the season. The players also deserve plenty of blame here. What is it going to take to motivate them to shed this image of the Jets being a bad franchise. Yes, Glenn is not a good head coach, but time and time again the players say the same garbage each week and never deliver. It's officially tiresome to listen to from the players. Stop talking about what you are going to do and just go out on the field and execute. Is it really that hard? Another season is officially over in October as the Jets now get ready to face the Las Vegas Raiders next week, a team with much more talent than Miami and a better head coach than Glenn. It's unfortunate that the team continues to put their fans through this each and every year. It would be nice if they actually cared about winning than picking in the Top 10 of the draft every year. This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: Report Card: Jets Lose To Miami 28-25 In Week 7

item.title: Kenneth Walker under fire for ignoring former Seahawks teammates after Chiefs first loss in 2026
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III faced off against his Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks teammates for the first time since leaving the squad. Walker III won Super Bowl MVP for his performances for the Seahawks to bring the city another Super Bowl title in 2026, but it did not guarantee his future with the franchise, as they chose to let him walk in free agency and join the Chiefs on a three-year, $43.05 million contract. Walker’s exit did not happen as amicably as either party would have liked, and it seems like the 26-year-old RB is still holding onto harsh feelings, as evidenced by the end of the Chiefs’ 20-3 loss to Seattle. Kenneth Walker snubs former Seahawks teammates after Chiefs loss After rushing for 14 carries and a season-low 36 yards, Walker went straight to the locker room after the game instead of shaking hands with his former teammates, who handed Kansas City their first loss of the season. Walker came under fire from NFL fans for doing this, especially after a one-sided loss. “That’s just sad, man. They didn’t mistreat him in his time in Seattle,” said one fan . “Bro saw Schneider lurking on the sidelines with his ballcap and suit and said nah,” said a fan, believing the presence of Seahawks President John Schneider caused Walker to run off. “I thought this was an odd exit. Why so salty?” questioned a fan . “That was a bad look. Kenneth has lots of friends on that team that truly love him. Why would he just run away? Bad sportsmanship on his part. I thought better of him than that. Very disappointing,” said another fan . “I’ll always love K9, but ya gotta be a man and shake your former teammates’ hands after getting smoked,” were the thoughts of another fan . Walker spent his final months as a Seahawk wondering if he would even get a contract offer from the franchise after winning Super Bowl MVP. He never wound up receiving one, with the Chiefs signing Walker on the first day of free agency. That outcome might have created bad feelings towards Schneider, who was also on the field at the end of the game. With Walker interacting with his teammates before the game, it is plausible he skipped the post-game handshakes to avoid interacting with the Seahawks President after how they parted ways. Walker has had a great start to the 2026 NFL season, rushing for 701 yards in 120 carries for six touchdowns while catching 18 receptions for 116 yards and two touchdowns. item.title: NFC playoff picture: Lions win to jump Packers
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions fumbles against the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images All of the NFC North teams are in the playoff picture. It’s that kind of year again. The Detroit Lions vaulted the Green Bay Packers by beating them in Week 7. The Minnesota Vikings are the only undefeated team in the NFL. The Chicago Bears pushed their record to 5-2 on Thursday night. The Lions are 4-2 and the Packers are 4-3. Currently, all the Wild Card teams are from the NFC North with the Seattle Seahawks just outside. Let’s take a closer look at the NFC playoff picture after Week 7, with “Monday Night Football” between the Eagles and Cowboys still to come. NFC North standings after Week 7 1. Minnesota Vikings (6-0) 2. Chicago Bears (5-2) 3. Detroit Lions (4-2) 4. Green Bay Packers (4-3) The Vikings continue to scoot by with an absolutely punishing defense, but an offense still desperate to find themselves. That makes them vulnerable, but someone has to figure out Brian Flores. All of their last five opponents have been held to 16 points or less. The Lions have the next crack at them, and Jared Goff has generally fared well vs. Minnesota, but last year Flores bested him. The Chicago Bears continue to look like the most well-rounded team. Their Thursday night win over the Patriots was just as much about their defense than it was Ben Johnson’s offense. But they’ve got a tough matchup in Seattle next week on Monday Night Football. The Lions are starting to look like a more balanced team, with the defense leading the way to victory against the Packers. While the injuries continue to mount for a Green Bay team that can’t seem to find an offensive identity outside of deep shots. NFC playoff standings after Week 7 Division leaders: 1. Minnesota Vikings (6-0) 2. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-3) Wild Card race (top three advance) 5. Chicago Bears (5-2) 6. Detroit Lions (4-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (4-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 9. Atlanta Falcons (3-4) 10. Los Angeles Rams (3-4) 11. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) – Monday Night Football 12. Dallas Cowboys (2-4) – Monday Night Football 13. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) 14. New Orleans Saints (2-5) 15. Arizona Cardinals (2-5) 16. Washington Commanders (1-4-1) While the Lions are two game behind in the division, they nearly have a two-game cushion in the Wild Card race. Of the teams behind them, only the Packers and Seahawks have three losses—the other eight teams have at least four. The Lions are also in pretty good standing when it comes to tiebreakers. Their current 3-1 record in conference games is only bested by the Vikings (4-0) and 49ers (4-1), and they haven’t yet dropped a divisional matchup.

item.title: Aleksandar Pavlović backs Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane and Michael Olise for Ballon d’Or
item.description: (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Aleksandar Pavlović is not afraid to dream big. The Bayern Munich midfielder has admitted that winning the Ballon d’Or is something he thinks about, while also throwing his support behind teammates Harry Kane and Michael Olise in the race for football’s most prestigious individua l award. Speaking to Sport Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Pavlović pointed to Rodri’s 2024 triumph as proof that defensive midfielders can rec eive the recognition their position deserves. “It’s nice to know that a defensive midfielder [Rodri] can win the Ballon d’Or. I’d be lying if I said it wouldn’t be my dream to win t he Ballon d’Or one day,” said Pavlović. For Pavlović, the dream is clearly there, even if he still has plenty of work ahead of him to reach that level. The 22-year-old has already established himself as an important part of Bayern Munich’s midfield, and continuing to develop under Vincent Kompany will be crucial to his ambitions. Of course, Pavlović also has two world-class teammates who could make a serious push for the award themselves. A sked whether he would prefer Kane or Olise to win the Ballon d’Or, the midfielder refused to pick a favorite. “For me, the most important thing is that one of them wins it as a Bayern Munich player. Both deserve it; they are outsta nding players. Harry and Michael help us win games week in, week out. So I’m rooting for both of them, ” Pavlović said. That is a sensible answer from Pavlović. Bayern Munich winning the Ballon d’Or would be a we lcome outcome, regardless of which star takes home the trophy. And if Pavlović keeps developing at his current pace, pe rhaps he can turn his own dream into reality someday. Join the conversation! item.content:encoded: (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Aleksandar Pavlović is not afraid to dream big. The Bayern Munich midfielder has admitted that winning the Ballon d’Or is something he thinks about, while also throwing his support behind teammates Harry Kane and Michael Olise in the race for football’s most prestigious individua l award. Speaking to Sport Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Pavlović pointed to Rodri’s 2024 triumph as proof that defensive midfielders can rec eive the recognition their position deserves. “It’s nice to know that a defensive midfielder [Rodri] can win the Ballon d’Or. I’d be lying if I said it wouldn’t be my dream to win t he Ballon d’Or one day,” said Pavlović. For Pavlović, the dream is clearly there, even if he still has plenty of work ahead of him to reach that level. The 22-year-old has already established himself as an important part of Bayern Munich’s midfield, and continuing to develop under Vincent Kompany will be crucial to his ambitions. Of course, Pavlović also has two world-class teammates who could make a serious push for the award themselves. A sked whether he would prefer Kane or Olise to win the Ballon d’Or, the midfielder refused to pick a favorite. “For me, the most important thing is that one of them wins it as a Bayern Munich player. Both deserve it; they are outsta nding players. Harry and Michael help us win games week in, week out. So I’m rooting for both of them, ” Pavlović said. That is a sensible answer from Pavlović. Bayern Munich winning the Ballon d’Or would be a we lcome outcome, regardless of which star takes home the trophy. And if Pavlović keeps developing at his current pace, pe rhaps he can turn his own dream into reality someday. Join the conversation! item.title: Cameron Boozer Update: Rolling Right Along
item.description: SACRAMENTO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 25: Cameron Boozer #27 of the Memphis Grizzlies is guarded by Precious Achiuwa #9 and Zach LaVine #8 of the Sacramento Kings during the second half at Golden 1 Center on October 25, 2026 in Sacramento, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images I t’s still early in the NBA season, but as we have noted, Cameron Boozer is off to a great start. Prior to Sunday night’s game, he was tied for third in the NBA in rebounding with 12 per game. He’s also averaging 16 points and 5.5 assists. On the downside, he’s not shooting that well, but rookies will be rookies. Against Sacramento on Sunday night , Boozer wound up with 16 points, 11 rebounds, and 4 assists, which is essentially right at his averages. More importantly, Memphis is 3-0. As for the players who went before him in the 2026 NBA Draft, #1 pick AJ Dybantsa hasn’t played yet due to injury, and the Washington Wizards are 2-1. The #2 pick, Darryn Peterson, is doing fairly well. He’s getting 12.0 ppg, 3.5 rebounds, and 2.0 assists. However, the Utah Jazz are just 1-2. It’s a long season, and things will obviously change, but as of now, Boozer is looking like the pick of the draft. item.title: Barcelona midfielder’s El Clasico omission raises fresh questions over his role at club
item.description: Barcelona midfielder’s El Clasico omission raises fresh questions over his role at club Gavi endured a significant setback in his difficult Barcelona season after Hansi Flick left him on the bench throughout the 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid. As per SPORT , it marked the first time the midfielder has missed an entire El Clasico through a coach’s selection decision since making his first-team debut. The 22-year-old had made no secret of his eagerness to face Barcelona’s fiercest rivals, but his competitive spirit counted for nothing when Flick decided against introducing him at the Spotify Camp Nou. More concerning than the omission itself is what it says about Gavi’s position in a midfield where opportunities are becoming increasingly difficult to find. For a player who has often thrived in the intensity of these fixtures, being unable to influence the contest was a particularly stark indication of how dramatically his circumstances have changed. Flick’s midfield hierarchy is becoming clearer Gavi had helped build anticipation for the Clasico with an emphatic assessment of what the fixture demands. “In Clasicos , you have to go to war. It doesn’t matter how either team is doing; these are do-or-die matches,” he said on Saturday. No minutes for Gavi in El Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Yet the midfielder was unable to translate that enthusiasm into an appearance. Although his omission from the starting lineup was not unexpected, the decision to leave him unused throughout the match was far more significant. Flick had already addressed Gavi’s situation in September, acknowledging the midfielder’s determination while emphasising the need to accept the team’s circumstances. “Gavi has great ambition and always wants to play. He played, got injured and then returned to playing, but the team is functioning as it is, and that has to be accepted,” the Barcelona manager explained. The challenge for Gavi is that the competition has become even tougher since those comments. Frenkie de Jong returned against Real Madrid, while Pedri and Rodri appear firmly established among Flick’s preferred midfield options. Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo provide further alternatives, and Marc Bernal has also featured in the competition for minutes. Losing prominence in the team. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) With so many players competing for a limited number of positions, Gavi risks slipping towards the bottom of the midfield rotation. A difficult situation Gavi’s current predicament is particularly frustrating given the physical difficulties he has had to overcome. The numbers underline the problem. Gavi has started only twice this season and has accumulated very limited playing time. His absence from the Clasico was therefore not an isolated incident, but the clearest indication yet of his diminished status. item.title: Can Eagles injured offense beat Cowboys D? Our experts score predictions
item.description: PHILADELPHIA − Something has got to give with one of the worst offenses in the NFL ( Eagles ) going against one of the worst defenses in the NFL (Cowboys) in a Monday Night Football game on Oct. 26. The Eagles' offense has proceeded to get only worse now that quarterback Jalen Hurts is lost for the season because of blood clots in both lungs, with Tanner McKee replacing him. And the Eagles will be without their top two wide receivers in DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, and running back Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable. So it's not like McKee has a full deck to work with. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets McKee was 26-for-45 for 215 yards in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Oct. 18. It was his third career NFL start. The game against the Cowboys will be his fourth. That is not the Eagles' only issue, of course. That explains why they're 2-4, having lost four straight. As a team, the Eagles have amassed fewer than 250 yards in each of their last four games. They're averaging 218.5 yards per game during that stretch. To put that in perspective, Tennessee is averaging a league-worst 236 yards per game this season. It's possible that left guard Landon Dickerson will come off injured reserve, and center Drew Kendall could return as well after missing two games with a knee injury. That will help, but only to an extent. The Eagles have scored just 3 points in the first quarter this season and 6 points in the third quarter under first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, whose new system doesn't seem to be working. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said "everything is on the table," in regard to fixing the offense, but then said Mannion will continue calling plays. And Mannion has doubled down on his confidence in that system working, even with the mostly immobile McKee replacing the mobile Hurts. "You look at a lot of the things that we need to improve, and I think they're totally fixable," Mannion said. "It's a double-edged sword, right? You look at [the results], and you can get frustrated by it. You can also look at that and put a silver lining on it and say, 'Man, if we just handle our simple stuff, we're going to yield a better result." The Cowboys defense could be the remedy. After all, the Cowboys are also 2-4 because their defense ranks last in rushing defense (150 yards allowed per game) and 30th in total yards allowed (383 yards per game). Then again, the Cowboys traded for cornerback Joey Porter, and Dallas' defense has improved since he joined the lineup two games ago. Plus, defensive tackle Quinnen Williams could be going against a banged-up Eagles interior line. And McKee isn't agile enough to escape. Here's how we see the game going: Our prognosticators are Martin Frank (Eagles beat writer/columnist, Delawareonline.com), Greg Giesen (sports strategist, Delawareonline.com), Tom McGurk (sports editor, Courierpostonline.com), Tom Moore (sports columnist, Phillyburbs.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, app.com), Bert Bainb

Here's how we see the game going: Our prognosticators are Martin Frank (Eagles beat writer/columnist, Delawareonline.com), Greg Giesen (sports strategist, Delawareonline.com), Tom McGurk (sports editor, Courierpostonline.com), Tom Moore (sports columnist, Phillyburbs.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, app.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter & columnist, Northjersey.com), Tom Haines (Pennsylvania state planning), Kevin Tresolini, (college sports reporter, Delawareonline.com), Michelle Ganassi (audience director & die-hard Steelers fan, Delawareonline.com), Tom Rimback (sports writer, Courierpostonline.com), Brandon Holveck (high school sports reporter, Delawareonline.com) Martin Frank The Eagles could be without edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith, and possibly Jalyx Hunt. If they can't get pressure on QB Dak Prescott, it could be a long night for the Eagles' secondary against WRs CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The only way the Eagles can pull this out is with a ball-control offense. If Barkley, Dickerson and Kendall are back, they can do it. The pick: Eagles 26, Cowboys 24 Greg Giesen Jalen Hurts is out for the season and Saquon Barkley hasn't played since Week 3. Thing is, it doesn't matter. The offensive line is porous. Even if Hurts and Barkley were there, the Eagles wouldn't be successful without the protection they've expected for years. And, without sustained drives on offense, the defense is gassed in the second half. The season is done. I'm sure the Eagles might win another game (I'm looking at you Arizona), but until the offensive line improves, it's hard to imagine a victory. And on Monday night at The Linc, expect an ugly evening as the hated Dallas Cowboys push the losing streak to five. The pick: Cowboys 24, Eagles 13 Kevin Tresolini The Eagles are at a low point, and lifting themselves out of it appears unlikely because those assigned the duties and paid the salaries to excel and win football games, coaches and players both, have utterly failed. And now comes a Monday night bout with despised Dallas for which it's difficult to summon any optimism the Eagles may actually rise to the occasion, despite the 2-4 Cowboys' own mediocrity. The pick: Cowboys 23, Eagles 16 Bob Jordan The line a week before this game had the Birds as almost a touchdown dog at home! Maybe that's motivation? The pick: Eagles 21, Cowboys 20 Tom Moore By late Monday night, the Eagles will have won all but five of their last five games. The pick: Cowboys 17, Eagles 13 Tom McGurk If there haven't been enough bad clouds hovering over the City of Brotherly Love lately, a loss to the rival Cowboys in the national spotlight will take the doom and gloom to another level. The pick: Cowboys 20, Eagles 13 Bert Bainbridge The Eagles score a few more points than they did against the Panthers, but it's still not enough as the Birds losing streak extends to five games for the first time in a decade. The pick: Cowboys 27, Eagles 17 Brandon Holveck The Eagles are in the wilderness, as am I, picking their games at a .500 clip so far this season. My belief in a semi-turnaround on offense has expired even as the Birds get set to face one of the league's worst defenses. The pick: Cowboys 23, Eagles 17 Tom Haines Yes, the Eagles will win again sometime this season, but it won't be Monday night. Tanner McKee and the patchwork offensive line are clearly not-ready-for-primetime players. The pick: Cowboys 23, Eagles 16 Michelle Ganassi I respectfully disagree with the group (well, most of the group). As a proud member of Steelers Nation, I know rivalries bring out something different, especially on a big stage. I’m taking the Eagles over the Cowboys, and I fully expect the memes afterward to be glorious. The pick: Eagles 14, Cowboys 7 Tom Rimback The who-are-these-guys Iggles face the predictably disappointing Cowboys on a Monday Night Football game that should open with an old-school rendition of Dandy Don Meridith singing 'Turn out the Lights.' What happens when the moveable object meets a resistible force? Who cares? item.title: Who slept worst last night: Lando Norris
item.description: Motorsport photo Amid all the admiration for Kimi Antonelli, whose world championship celebrations in Austin on Sunday evening had to be put on ice until Mexico, one rather significant development in the 2026 Formula 1 season almost slipped under the radar: the first major verdict has been delivered. George Russell and Lewis Hamilton may still be in the title race, at least mathematically. But one driver has officially been eliminated. After 18 of the 23 scheduled Grands Prix, Lando Norris trails Antonelli, the champion-in-waiting beyond any reasonable doubt, by 154 points. Yet with Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi still to come, there are only 125 points left on the table for any individual driver. Read Also: Winners and losers from F1's United States Grand Prix Which means his reign as Formula 1 world champion is officially over. And the coveted number 1, which he had waited so long to carry on his car, now has just a few more weeks left before its farewell tour comes to an end. In truth, it had been clear for quite some time that the 26-year-old was unlikely to defend his crown. As early as the season opener in Melbourne, the writing was on the wall: Mercedes would be an extraordinarily tough nut to crack in 2026. It took until the fourth race of the season, in Miami, for Norris to even make his first podium appearance. Then, in July, McLaren introduced an upgrade that arrived (too?) late but nevertheless offered a tantalising glimpse of a possible return to former glory. Norris won in Hungary, just before the summer break, and again in the Netherlands immediately afterwards. And although it was already becoming increasingly obvious that retaining the title was probably beyond his reach, plenty of observers still had him pencilled in as a potential runner-up in the championship. Myself included, I must admit. Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren We now know that Hungary and Zandvoort were little more than a flash in the pan. The McLaren-Mercedes MCL40 is by no means an inherently slow racing car. But unpredictability is hardwired into its DNA. Or, to borrow Norris's own explanation: you nail three corners on a lap, then tweak the set-up to improve the next three. And sure enough, those next three corners get better. The trouble is, the balance that made the first three work so beautifully has suddenly vanished. A classic case of fixing one problem only to create another. Singapore then marked a new low on Norris's road to dethronement. In the F1 Sprint, of all places, he managed to drive into his own team-mate Oscar Piastri , earning himself several stern lectures in the process. Behind closed doors, naturally. You would hardly expect anything else from a team run by Andrea Stella. But the message, it seems, hit home. It was an incident that may well have left its mark on the relationship between Norris, long perceived by fans as McLaren's undisputed golden boy, and the team he has called home for so many years. Lando Norr
item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Amid all the admiration for Kimi Antonelli, whose world championship celebrations in Austin on Sunday evening had to be put on ice until Mexico, one rather significant development in the 2026 Formula 1 season almost slipped under the radar: the first major verdict has been delivered. George Russell and Lewis Hamilton may still be in the title race, at least mathematically. But one driver has officially been eliminated. After 18 of the 23 scheduled Grands Prix, Lando Norris trails Antonelli, the champion-in-waiting beyond any reasonable doubt, by 154 points. Yet with Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi still to come, there are only 125 points left on the table for any individual driver. Read Also: Winners and losers from F1's United States Grand Prix Which means his reign as Formula 1 world champion is officially over. And the coveted number 1, which he had waited so long to carry on his car, now has just a few more weeks left before its farewell tour comes to an end. In truth, it had been clear for quite some time that the 26-year-old was unlikely to defend his crown. As early as the season opener in Melbourne, the writing was on the wall: Mercedes would be an extraordinarily tough nut to crack in 2026. It took until the fourth race of the season, in Miami, for Norris to even make his first podium appearance. Then, in July, McLaren introduced an upgrade that arrived (too?) late but nevertheless offered a tantalising glimpse of a possible return to former glory. Norris won in Hungary, just before the summer break, and again in the Netherlands immediately afterwards. And although it was already becoming increasingly obvious that retaining the title was probably beyond his reach, plenty of observers still had him pencilled in as a potential runner-up in the championship. Myself included, I must admit. Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren We now know that Hungary and Zandvoort were little more than a flash in the pan. The McLaren-Mercedes MCL40 is by no means an inherently slow racing car. But unpredictability is hardwired into its DNA. Or, to borrow Norris's own explanation: you nail three corners on a lap, then tweak the set-up to improve the next three. And sure enough, those next three corners get better. The trouble is, the balance that made the first three work so beautifully has suddenly vanished. A classic case of fixing one problem only to create another. Singapore then marked a new low on Norris's road to dethronement. In the F1 Sprint, of all places, he managed to drive into his own team-mate Oscar Piastri , earning himself several stern lectures in the process. Behind closed doors, naturally. You would hardly expect anything else from a team run by Andrea Stella. But the message, it seems, hit home. It was an incident that may well have left its mark on the relationship between Norris, long perceived by fans as McLaren's undisputed golden boy, and the team he has called home for so many years. Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren Norris has never been the sort of driver who radiates unshakeable self-confidence every waking moment. Not in the way Max Verstappen does, for example. And yet, for much of the 2026 season, he had seemed remarkably at peace with himself. Comfortable in his own skin, secure in the knowledge that he had already ticked off the one great ambition of his life. Last weekend, however, something felt different. Two weeks after Singapore and the dressing-downs that apparently followed, Norris seemed a changed man. Gone was the occasionally ironic sense of humour he normally brings to interviews. And over the team radio during the race, there were moments when he sounded almost intimidated. Uncertain of himself. Like a small child who has just been given a proper telling-off by his parents and no longer dares to speak his mind, even when he secretly believes he is right. Take the early stages of the race at the Circuit of the Americas. Norris was running behind Piastri, clearly had more pace than his team-mate, and was asked just how much faster he could actually go. Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren An invitation to engineer a position swap, if ever there was one. The natural racing driver's instinct would have been to fire back something along the lines of "at least four tenths". Instead, Norris mumbled almost apologetically into his radio: "Yeah, I mean ... Yeah. I'm being held up now. I'm closer to him than he is apparently." Later in the race, as Norris attempted to nurse his worn tyres to the finish without another pit stop, his team advised him to come in after detecting a flat spot. His response? "I don't have a flatspot. But you can do whatever you want." And later still, he went as far as saying: "No more calls, please." There was no aggression in his voice. No outright anger, either. But there was defiance. The kind of quiet, stubborn defiance that speaks volumes precisely because it is so restrained. Norris had retreated into monosyllabic communication, saying little more than the bare minimum. We have all been there. When my partner is getting so spectacularly on my nerves that I am quietly boiling on the inside, but I know full well that speaking my mind would trigger an argument in which I might completely lose my temper, I behave in exactly the same way. Short answers. Tight lips. No unnecessary conversation. Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren All the while knowing perfectly well that the person on the other side knows exactly what is going on beneath the surface. Perhaps, though, all of this is happening at precisely the right time. A storm that clears the air, at a moment when both Norris and McLaren can afford to let the thunder roll. Remember Nico Rosberg in 2015? After a season that had gone badly off the rails, he started winning again in Mexico and went on to string together one victory after another. And we all know how that story ended in 2016. Some Formula 1 world champions possess an almost mystical aura of invincibility. Ayrton Senna was one of them. When backmarkers caught sight of that famous yellow helmet in their mirrors, they practically moved aside in reverence as he came through to lap them. Because they knew just how uncompromising Senna could be. Or take Verstappen. Even Lewis Hamilton, of all people, regularly thinks twice before going wheel-to-wheel with him. Because everyone knows that, when push comes to shove, Max is perfectly prepared to let things get ugly. Norris does not possess that aura. He is not the kind of man who takes his insecurities to bed, wrestles with them behind closed doors and makes absolutely certain that the outside world never sees a crack in his armour. Quite the opposite. His willingness to be open about his doubts and vulnerabilities is precisely what makes him so immensely likeable as a human being. But perhaps it also leaves him just that little bit more exposed. A little easier to unsettle. A little more vulnerable to those who know where to press. So what will his career ultimately look like? Will he join the ranks of Senna and Verstappen, drivers who turned one world championship into several? Or will his story end up looking rather more like Jenson Button's: one glorious, unforgettable season at the very summit of Formula 1, followed by years in which that ultimate triumph never quite came within reach again? Read Also: Who slept best last night: Liam Lawson F1 United States GP: Kimi Antonelli takes dominant victory - but no title A great deal of that, of course, will depend on the car beneath him. But perhaps a small part of the answer also lies elsewhere. In learning to develop a thicker skin. In becoming a little more resilient, a little harder to rattle. And in discovering that, sometimes, when someone is angry with you, the best response is simply to shr

item.title: ‘She deserves respect’: Swifties not happy after NFL team mocks Taylor Swift
item.description: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Seattle Seahawks handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss of the season on Sunday night, and then decided to take a shot at Travis Kelce’s wife, Taylor Swift. As you might expect, the Swifties were not too happy about it. After the 20-3 win, the Seahawks posted a friendship bracelet that read “Seahawks Win,” with a caption referencing one of Swift’s songs. And plenty of Swift fans were quick to voice their displeasure on social media. The Seahawks’ Troll Seattle’s defense dominated Kansas City on Sunday Night Football , holding the Chiefs to just 213 total yards in the game. Swift appeared to skip the game, as she was not shown on the NBC broadcast, according to the New York Post . However, that didn’t stop the Seahawks from mocking her and Kelce after the game. Following the win, the team’s official account shared a photo of a friendship bracelet spelling out “Seahawks Win,” with the caption “End Game,” a track from Swift’s 2017 album reputation . End Game https://t.co/fUGMpcCMjX — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 The post was a reference to the friendship bracelets Swift’s fans traded at her Eras Tour concerts. It’s also a subtle reference to the couple’s love story, since Kelce famously tried to give Swift a bracelet with his number on it at one of her shows in 2023, as ESPN noted . ‘Leave Taylor Out Of This’ Needless to say, the loyal and passionate Swifties were not too fond of the Seahawks taking a shot at Taylor. “Why do y’all think it’s okay to troll a team by using the spouse of an opposing player? This wouldn’t be acceptable if she wasn’t Taylor Swift. She deserves respect just like every other player’s spouse,” one fan wrote . “The disrespect is why I hate other teams, make it a chief pun, but why Taylor why a spouse, they wouldn’t make fun of Claire Kittle or Kelly [Stafford] so why is this okay?” another fan wrote . “whether you think it’s cute or not. why are we bringing players significant others into this? taylor did not play, she wasn’t even there and you use her song as a caption,” another fan added . “Sorry but this is not it and other teams were called out this one cant be the exception, Taylor has nothing to do with this beyond being married to Travis,” another Swift fan wrote . “And while I was rooting for you guys last year just like that my respect for you is gone. Hope rest of your season sucks bc this is just tasteless,” one fan replied . “Seattle on the hatewatch for the rest of the season now. LEAVE TAYLOR OUT OF THIS,” one fan wrote . Clearly, the Seahawks may have made some new enemies. item.title: Arch Manning and Texas get more bad news despite win over Ole Miss
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) throws a pass during the second half against the Mississippi Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns finally got a much-needed win on Saturday night, holding off No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 to snap a two-game losing streak. While it was a big win for the team in what was essentially a must-win game for their College Football Playoff hopes, it came with a price. Texas will now reportedly be without star left tackle Trevor Goosby for the rest of the season after he suffered a knee injury in the win. That means Manning, who was under plenty of pressure before the game, just lost the player responsible for protecting his blind side. Goosby Out For Season Goosby was carted off the field in the first half and was later spotted on the sideline on crutches. After the game, Sarkisian said that neither Goosby’s injury nor wide receiver Cam Coleman’s shoulder injury “looked very good,” via Yahoo Sports . On Sunday, the news on Goosby was confirmed to be as bad as feared. “Sources: Texas star left tackle Trevor Goosby will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury against Ole Miss on Saturday,” wrote ESPN’s Pete Thamel . “Goosby is the country’s top NFL prospect at left tackle, as ESPN’s Field Yates ranked him the No. 8 pick in his most recent mock draft.” Goosby returned to Texas for his senior season and was a preseason first-team All-American. A Rough Stretch For Manning Manning entered the season as a Heisman Trophy favorite, but back-to-back 27-24 losses to Oklahoma and Florida had him on the verge of getting benched, especially after he had two costly turnovers late in each of those games. After the loss to Florida, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian did not rule out benching Manning, and Texas reportedly started to prepare for a potential quarterback change last week, and Sarkisian warned Manning that he would make a change unless he improved. Manning answered with three total touchdowns against Ole Miss. However, the offense did slow down significantly after Goosby’s injury as Manning also had three turnovers, including a fumble on Texas’ first possession of the second half that came under pressure from the side of the line that Goosby usually protects. ‘The Ultimate Team Sport’ Even before the injury, Texas was already shorthanded, playing without pass rusher Colin Simmons and running back Hollywood Smothers. Things only got more difficult when Goosby and star wide receiver Coleman left the game with injuries. But Texas won the game anyway. “I’d be remiss if I didn’t say, this is the ultimate team sport,” Sarkisian said after the game, via On3 . “We played without Colin Simmons. We played without Hollywood Smothers. “We essentially played the entire game without Trevor Goosby, and the majority of the game without Cam Coleman, and we played the number seven ranked team

item.title: Maryland men’s basketball’s frontcourt will be defined by Pharrel Payne — but there’s help
item.description: With the leaves turning in color and the days shortening, the weather outside is harkening the start of the hoops season, when Maryland men’s basketball will hope to make a big turnaround in year two of head coach Buzz Williams’ regime. With two preseason exhibitions and a secret scrimmage in the books, attention now turns to Nov. 2, when Maryland welcomes Bucknell to Xfinity Center to officially kick off the 2026-27 season. The Terps’ roster saw heavy turnover, with just four players returning for another year under Williams. To count down to the start of the regular season, Testudo Times will be previewing the Terps’ frontcourt, backcourt and freshmen before offering their predictions for the season’s outlook. House of Payne This time last year, Maryland had just four healthy forwards — and two of them were Collin Metcalf and Aleks Alston, who didn’t contribute much over the course of the season. Now, Maryland has twice as many options to run the rim and dominate the boards. For forward Pharrel Payne, another of last year’s early options who asserted himself early in the year, the extra competition is a good thing. “A lot of relief there,” Payne said, “just knowing and looking to my side that I got a guy that’s always going to be on the court with me that can help as well as guys on the bench that are coming off the bench ready to play.” The biggest offseason question mark for Maryland was the status of its star forward. At the team’s media day, Payne said he only became fully sure of his extra year of eligibility shortly before this offseason’s summer workouts. While the paperwork process left it late, Maryland never outwardly doubted the chances of Payne’s return. His return raises its floor and ceiling. The 6-foot-9 Payne averaged 17.5 points and 7.2 rebounds per game and was unquestionably Maryland’s best player for the 10 games he was able to play. He was one of 11 players named to the preseason all-Big Ten team this season and will be a legitimate All-American candidate if Maryland meets its potential this season. Experienced contributors enter New Mexico transfer Tomislav Buljan is expected to be Payne’s primary partner in the frontcourt and should be an instant upgrade on anything the Terps had in the position last season. The 23-year-old Croatian is listed as a sophomore entering his second season in the United States. He was a professional in his home country and Spain from 2021-25, bringing a trove of experience with him to New Mexico last season. item.content:encoded: With the leaves turning in color and the days shortening, the weather outside is harkening the start of the hoops season, when Maryland men’s basketball will hope to make a big turnaround in year two of head coach Buzz Williams’ regime. With two preseason exhibitions and a secret scrimmage in the books, attention now turns to Nov. 2, when Maryland welcomes Bucknell to Xfinity Center to officially kick off the 2026-27 season. The Terps’ roster saw heavy turnover, with just four players returning for another year under Williams. To count down to the start of the regular season, Testudo Times will be previewing the Terps’ frontcourt, backcourt and freshmen before offering their predictions for the season’s outlook. House of Payne This time last year, Maryland had just four healthy forwards — and two of them were Collin Metcalf and Aleks Alston, who didn’t contribute much over the course of the season. Now, Maryland has twice as many options to run the rim and dominate the boards. For forward Pharrel Payne, another of last year’s early options who asserted himself early in the year, the extra competition is a good thing. “A lot of relief there,” Payne said, “just knowing and looking to my side that I got a guy that’s always going to be on the court with me that can help as well as guys on the bench that are coming off the bench ready to play.” The biggest offseason question mark for Maryland was the status of its star forward. At the team’s media day, Payne said he only became fully sure of his extra year of eligibility shortly before this offseason’s summer workouts. While the paperwork process left it late, Maryland never outwardly doubted the chances of Payne’s return. His return raises its floor and ceiling. The 6-foot-9 Payne averaged 17.5 points and 7.2 rebounds per game and was unquestionably Maryland’s best player for the 10 games he was able to play. He was one of 11 players named to the preseason all-Big Ten team this season and will be a legitimate All-American candidate if Maryland meets its potential this season. Experienced contributors enter New Mexico transfer Tomislav Buljan is expected to be Payne’s primary partner in the frontcourt and should be an instant upgrade on anything the Terps had in the position last season. The 23-year-old Croatian is listed as a sophomore entering his second season in the United States. He was a professional in his home country and Spain from 2021-25, bringing a trove of experience with him to New Mexico last season. Buljan averaged 13 points and 10 rebounds per game while in the Mountain West with the Lobos and snagged a school-record 141 offensive rebounds. His steady double-doubles were founded on efficiency — he has shot 48% or better from the field since turning professional. In his lone public preseason appearance with Maryland, Buljan went 0-of-6 from the field but grabbed seven rebounds, earning the Terps valuable possessions. While his offensive abilities are comparatively limited, his ability to recycle the ball and physicality — which Payne said is “borderline the same” as his — have earned rave reviews from Williams and company. While there was comparatively less fanfare around the offseason arrival of Robert Jennings II from Oklahoma State, he will likely get significant minutes as an energetic rotation piece. Like Payne, Jennings earned a medical redshirt after getting hurt early last season, so the best frame of reference for him is two years ago. While playing for the Cowboys in 2024-25, he averaged 5.4 points and 3.4 rebounds in 16.5 minutes per game. He excelled at drawing fouls and defending, which aligns perfectly with Williams’ philosophy. “One thing Coach Buzz always emphasizes to me is that I do a lot of things good, and he says that because you can put me on the floor with a lot of different people in a lot of different positions,” Jennings said. “I’ve played the five in college at a high major program, so I’ve had to figure out how to be an undersized big, but also I’m agile and athletic enough where if I have to switch on a two or three or one, you can also do that with me.” There is perhaps no greater indicator of the Terps’ depth difference than George Turkson Jr., who had double-digit minutes in 14 games last season and started in four Big Ten games but may struggle to see the court consistently in 2026-27. Turkson was serviceable when called upon to play spot minutes at center or either forward spot; his presence may be appreciated more as the Terps wade into a dense Big Ten slate. Bets on big upside While the Terps’ top three forwards will be out of eligibility after this season, Maryland invested heavily in the frontcourt when recruiting. Freshmen Baba Oladotun, Austin Brown and Adama Tambedou could be useful players for Maryland both this season and in the years to come. Oladotun entered the season with the hype for Maryland, but he struggled to make an impact in Maryland’s two public preseason games. He played just two minutes across the second half and overtime of the Terps’ game against West Virginia, and expectations may need to be tempered as the 17-year-old adjusts to the physicality of the college game. Brown and Tambedou, meanwhile, looked more ready to make an instant impact in their limited minutes. Brown gives the Terps a legitimate 3-and-D option on the wing, while Tambedou has immense size and aggression on the interior. For more analysis on the first-years, Testudo Times’ freshmen-specific preview will come out later this week. The last addition to Maryland’s roster, Alex K’Medehouto, is also its biggest mystery. The 7-foot junior averaged 3.8 points and 5.4 rebounds per game at the junior college level over the last two years and earned the step up to Maryland. He figures to be a break-glass-in-emergency option to fill out the bench, something the Terps found themselves desperately wishing for last season — but look far from needing this time around.

item.title: Knicks Have Issues To Sort Amid 0-3 Start
item.description: New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) reacts after getting called for a foul in the fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic at Madison Square Garden. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The New York Knicks became the first defending champions to start 0-3 since the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks after falling to the Orlando Magic 111-102 on Sunday night. Losing to the Philadelphia 76ers is understandable, as is losing to the Boston Celtics . Philadelphia and Boston are considered top contenders in the Eastern Conference. But losing to an Orlando team without Paolo Banchero is a different story. Here are some concerning observations about New York’s rocky start. The offense is way too Sloppy One of the Knicks’ greatest strengths last season was their offensive prowess and chemistry. They almost always made the right pass and took the right shot. It was one of the team’s aspects that led many to believe they had a good shot at successfully defending their title. However, that has not been the case this season, and definitely was not the case on Sunday. For one, there are just too many missed shots, particularly from beyond the arc. Before Sunday, New York was shooting 37% from three. Against Orlando, they shot an abysmal 24%. Karl-Anthony Towns went 0-4. Jalen Brunson went 1-7, with his lone made three-pointer coming late in the fourth quarter when the game was already beyond reach. Josh Hart went 3-9. Constantly hitting the iron is not a recipe for success, especially on a night when the opponent shot 43% from three. But the offensive issues are more than just missed threes. Turnovers have been killing this team. The turnovers keep the Knicks on a self-imposed leash, allowing teams to stay in games the way Orlando did tonight. Orlando scored 23 points off of New York’s 16 turnovers, which was one of the differences in the game. The Knicks tend to turn the ball over most often when they make an extra pass. Making an extra pass can usually be a great aspect of an offense. But the Knicks are not just making one extra pass — they make an extra two, three extra passes. In search of the “perfect” shot, they are constantly passing up good looks right there. It makes all five players on the court at a given time too passive on offense. And Sunday night was no exception. Mikal Bridges is Invisible New York Knicks shooting guard Mikal Bridges (25) reacts during the first half against the Toronto Raptors at Madison Square Garden. item.content:encoded: New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) reacts after getting called for a foul in the fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic at Madison Square Garden. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The New York Knicks became the first defending champions to start 0-3 since the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks after falling to the Orlando Magic 111-102 on Sunday night. Losing to the Philadelphia 76ers is understandable, as is losing to the Boston Celtics . Philadelphia and Boston are considered top contenders in the Eastern Conference. But losing to an Orlando team without Paolo Banchero is a different story. Here are some concerning observations about New York’s rocky start. The offense is way too Sloppy One of the Knicks’ greatest strengths last season was their offensive prowess and chemistry. They almost always made the right pass and took the right shot. It was one of the team’s aspects that led many to believe they had a good shot at successfully defending their title. However, that has not been the case this season, and definitely was not the case on Sunday. For one, there are just too many missed shots, particularly from beyond the arc. Before Sunday, New York was shooting 37% from three. Against Orlando, they shot an abysmal 24%. Karl-Anthony Towns went 0-4. Jalen Brunson went 1-7, with his lone made three-pointer coming late in the fourth quarter when the game was already beyond reach. Josh Hart went 3-9. Constantly hitting the iron is not a recipe for success, especially on a night when the opponent shot 43% from three. But the offensive issues are more than just missed threes. Turnovers have been killing this team. The turnovers keep the Knicks on a self-imposed leash, allowing teams to stay in games the way Orlando did tonight. Orlando scored 23 points off of New York’s 16 turnovers, which was one of the differences in the game. The Knicks tend to turn the ball over most often when they make an extra pass. Making an extra pass can usually be a great aspect of an offense. But the Knicks are not just making one extra pass — they make an extra two, three extra passes. In search of the “perfect” shot, they are constantly passing up good looks right there. It makes all five players on the court at a given time too passive on offense. And Sunday night was no exception. Mikal Bridges is Invisible New York Knicks shooting guard Mikal Bridges (25) reacts during the first half against the Toronto Raptors at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Another game, another ghost performance from Mikal Bridges . After scoring only four points in the opener and not scoring at all in Boston on Friday, he finished with just six points on seven attempts over 35 minutes. He had an abysmal plus-minus of -21, far and away the worst from any player on either team. It looks like Bridges lost a bit of confidence in his game. Bridges is playing much more passively and is hesitant to commit to an offensive decision fully. And on the defensive side, he often looked lost amid the Magic’s three-point barrage. Bridges has gone through such stretches with the Knicks before, most notably during Games 2 and 3 of the first-round series against the Atlanta Hawks last season. Bridges did not score in the second half of Game 2, including missing a game-winning shot, and didn’t score at all in Game 3. But he made it out on the other side and became one of the most integral pieces to the Knicks’ success. But he’s going to have to find any port in the storm sooner rather than later. Jalen Brunson Hasn’t Been Captain Clutch Lately New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) celebrates with center James Wiseman (35) after an Orlando Magic timeout in the second quarter at Madison Square Garden. Photo Credit: Wendell Cruz, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Brunson is known across the league and to most fans as the most clutch player in the game right now. The 2025 Clutch Player of the Year has risen to the occasion, saving the Knicks when they needed him most. This was especially the case in the closeout Game 5 of the NBA Finals, when he scored 45 points to clinch the title for New York. But that version of Jalen Brunson has yet to be seen this season. Brunson only scored six fourth-quarter points over the first two games, which was already raising alarm bells. Sunday night raised them even more. Brunson had nine points in the fourth on Sunday, but seven of those came inside the final 33 seconds when the win was already beyond reach. Before that, he turned the ball over twice, missed two field goals, and missed both free throws during his first trip to the stripe. It was an abysmal performance in every sense of the word. The Knicks cannot and will not win if he keeps playing like this. The Last Word on Knicks Winless Start The Knicks are still one of the elite teams in the NBA. There’s a reason the Larry O’Brien Trophy currently resides on 33rd & 7th. But the status as the hunted is not something to be taken lightly. Every team will treat their game against the Knicks as the most important on the schedule. And while the Knicks sleepwalked through the first week of the season, they saw the best efforts from three different Eastern Conference teams, all of whom thoroughly outplayed them in their respective games. The offense needs to clean up its turnover bug and start making its threes. Bridges needs to push through this rough stretch. And Brunson’s fourth-quarter shots need to start hitting the nylon. They are more than capable of overcoming all of these issues, but in an extra-competitive East, they need to do so with urgency. item.title: Farke explains Leeds United star’s absence in draw with Sunderland
item.description: Farke explains Leeds United star’s absence in draw with Sunderland Daniel Farke revealed Nico Elvedi was forced to miss Leeds United’s goalless draw with Sunderland after falling ill overnight. With Joe Rodon already sidelined, Elvedi’s late withdrawal left Leeds short of options at the back ahead of a difficult afternoon at the Stadium of Light. “Joe Rodon is out anyway,” Farke said. “Nico Elvedi missed the game overnight due to illness and felt unwell. He had to travel back.” Farke also felt the difficult weather conditions affected the quality of the game and praised his players for adapting. “And then weather conditions where you could hardly predict the curve of the ball,” he said. “It was one of those days where you have to accept that you can’t shine that much football-wise. “It’s more or less to dig in and grind out a result and fight for second balls and show steel. “And this is what we did today.”

item.title: Barca's big-game defeats pose familiar questions
item.description: Barcelona suffered defeats by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid to pose questions about their ability on the biggest occasions (Lluis GENE) After a superb start to the season Barcelona were brought crashing back down to earth by Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain last week, raising fresh doubts about the Spanish champions' ability to compete against the strongest opponents. Hansi Flick's side have dominated in Spain over the last two seasons, winning back-to-back La Liga titles, but notably in Europe have fallen short on high-pressure nights. The Catalan giants have played sumptuous attacking football this season and won their first 11 games across all competitions, but once the quality of their opponents rose, it was a different story. Barca were beaten 4-2 in Paris by European champions PSG on Tuesday, showing they are still some way from matching Luis Enrique's side. That was compounded by Sunday's painful 2-1 home defeat by Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid in La Liga, in which Barcelona's defensive frailties were laid bare again. A draw would have been an acceptable result and maintained their six-point lead on Madrid in the top flight, but they left far too much space for Los Blancos to exploit in the final stages. With three minutes to go Eduardo Camavinga raced through on goal and squared for Kylian Mbappe to net his 100th Madrid goal and second of the night to snatch victory. "In the end sometimes in the big, big games, small things are important and they decide the game and which way they end, and today that was not on our side," Flick told reporters, pledging to improve. "We know what we have to make better. We speak about this in every training. We will do it, I'm not worried about that. "It's a part of this game to lose also. In this week, we had two (losses) and it's too much." However it is a discourse which the German coach has repeated during his tenure. "We are a young side and we have to mature," said Flick, after Inter Milan ousted Barcelona in the Champions League semi-finals in May 2025. "We are working on it and we have to improve in defence and in other aspects." - Lack of 'freshness' - Despite spending good money on Anthony Gordon, Rodri and others this summer, and trying to bring in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez, Barcelona did not sign a centre-back. Instead Flick has persisted with Gerard Martin, a converted left-back, playing alongside Pau Cubarsi. Martin has done well, considering his technical limitations and change of position, but against the world's best strikers is clearly out of his depth. The defender's poor clearance handed Madrid their first goal against Barca, with Mbappe gleefully capitalising.
