item.content:encoded: Barcelona suffered defeats by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid to pose questions about their ability on the biggest occasions (Lluis GENE) After a superb start to the season Barcelona were brought crashing back down to earth by Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain last week, raising fresh doubts about the Spanish champions' ability to compete against the strongest opponents. Hansi Flick's side have dominated in Spain over the last two seasons, winning back-to-back La Liga titles, but notably in Europe have fallen short on high-pressure nights. The Catalan giants have played sumptuous attacking football this season and won their first 11 games across all competitions, but once the quality of their opponents rose, it was a different story. Barca were beaten 4-2 in Paris by European champions PSG on Tuesday, showing they are still some way from matching Luis Enrique's side. That was compounded by Sunday's painful 2-1 home defeat by Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid in La Liga, in which Barcelona's defensive frailties were laid bare again. A draw would have been an acceptable result and maintained their six-point lead on Madrid in the top flight, but they left far too much space for Los Blancos to exploit in the final stages. With three minutes to go Eduardo Camavinga raced through on goal and squared for Kylian Mbappe to net his 100th Madrid goal and second of the night to snatch victory. "In the end sometimes in the big, big games, small things are important and they decide the game and which way they end, and today that was not on our side," Flick told reporters, pledging to improve. "We know what we have to make better. We speak about this in every training. We will do it, I'm not worried about that. "It's a part of this game to lose also. In this week, we had two (losses) and it's too much." However it is a discourse which the German coach has repeated during his tenure. "We are a young side and we have to mature," said Flick, after Inter Milan ousted Barcelona in the Champions League semi-finals in May 2025. "We are working on it and we have to improve in defence and in other aspects." - Lack of 'freshness' - Despite spending good money on Anthony Gordon, Rodri and others this summer, and trying to bring in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez, Barcelona did not sign a centre-back. Instead Flick has persisted with Gerard Martin, a converted left-back, playing alongside Pau Cubarsi. Martin has done well, considering his technical limitations and change of position, but against the world's best strikers is clearly out of his depth. The defender's poor clearance handed Madrid their first goal against Barca, with Mbappe gleefully capitalising. To Martin's credit, he did defend well to stop Jude Bellingham and Mbappe in a two-on-one situation early in the second half, which exposed a more structural problem Barca have. Their high-line defence is easy to breach when the team's pressing is not executed perfectly, with high energy. Flick suggested Barcelona lacked "freshness" against Madrid, after a gruelling schedule, although his team had an extra day to recover midweek and the coach waited until the final minutes to introduce Gabriel Jesus and Karim Adeyemi. Barca do have injury problems at the back, with Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde and Andreas Christensen all missing the Clasico, along with midfielder Dani Olmo. "This may be the most important point, the injuries we have," explained Flick. Barcelona still hold a three-point lead on Madrid, third, in the title race. They are more than capable of going on another run of victories, but the weeks ahead will pose further interesting tests. Aston Villa visit Camp Nou in the Champions League on November 3, before Barcelona head to Atletico Madrid on November 8. A month after that, Manchester City come to the Camp Nou. Flick has been promising improvement in these type of matches for over two years -- perhaps now he will finally focus on implementing it. rbs/mw

item.title: Celtics' Win Over Knicks Featured a Stunning Zero From New York Starter
item.description: Celtics' Win Over Knicks Featured a Stunning Zero From New York Starter originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum deserved plenty of attention after leading the Boston Celtics to a 107-103 victory over the New York Knicks on Friday night. The Boston star finished with 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, helping the Celtics recover from their season-opening loss to Detroit. But another number from the game tells an equally interesting story. Zero. That's how many points New York forward Mikal Bridges scored in nearly 22 minutes against Boston. For a Knicks team trying to defend its NBA championship, the performance was an unexpected development in a game decided by only four points. A Surprising Night for Bridges Bridges finished 0-for-8 from the field, including 0-for-5 from three-point range. He recorded four assists, one rebound and one steal, but couldn't find a way to put the ball in the basket. It was a particularly frustrating performance because New York received significant contributions elsewhere. Mikal Bridges as Knicks lose in Boston 107-103: 0 points 0-8 shooting 0-5 three 0 free throws https://t.co/8AdLsvxlfw — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 24, 2026 Karl-Anthony Towns scored 22 points and grabbed 10 rebounds. OG Anunoby added 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists, while Miles McBride supplied 20 points off the bench. McBride was especially dangerous from the perimeter, connecting on six of his eight three-point attempts. Yet the Knicks still couldn't overcome Boston. Bridges' struggles weren't the only reason. New York also committed 18 turnovers, seven more than the Celtics, and failed to complete its late comeback. Still, an eight-shot, scoreless performance from a prominent member of the starting lineup stands out in such a narrow defeat. Had Bridges converted even a few of his opportunities, the final result might have looked different. Boston Won Without Dominating Every Category The Celtics didn't control every aspect of Friday's game. New York won the rebounding battle 44-37 and made 16 three-pointers compared with Boston's 15. The Knicks also recorded more assists, finishing with 27 to the Celtics' 25. Those numbers make the result particularly interesting. Boston found a way to win despite losing several statistical categories that often help determine the outcome of close games. The Celtics protected the basketball better, capitalized on New York's mistakes and leaned on Tatum when the game became uncomfortable. Tatum's late scoring helped prevent the Knicks from completing their comeback. His performance was the obvious headline, but Boston's ability to take advantage of New York's uneven offensive production also played a major role. The Celtics received 15 points apiece from Paul George and Neemias Queta, while Derrick White contributed 12 points and six assists. It wasn't a flawless team performance, but it was enough. item.title: Official: Como hand new contract extension to top goalscorer Douvikas
item.description: Official: Como hand new contract extension to top goalscorer Douvikas Como have officially announced that the club’s top goalscorer Tasos Douvikas has put pen to paper on a new long-term contract that will see him through until the summer of 2031. Official: Como tie down Douvikas until 2031 The Greece international had already been tied to a contract that was due to expire in the summer of 2029, but has seen his deal extended after an excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign, which has brought eight goals from 11 appearances at club level thus far. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Tasos Douvikas scores his team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Douvikas is Como’s leading goalscorer across all competitions and in each individual competition with five goals from eight appearances in Serie A and three from three in the Champions League. He finished the 2025-26 season with 14 goals in Serie A: A tally only bettered by Capocannoniere Lautaro Martinez (17). Douvikas has now scored 27 goals and provided five assists from 68 appearances across all competitions since joining Como from Celta Vigo in February of 2025. “I’m very happy to continue my journey with Como; I’ve felt right at home from the very beginning and immediately sensed the club’s ambition,” said Douvikas in a statement on the club website. “I’ve grown a lot since I arrived, thanks to Coach Fàbregas and his staff, this group is like a big family to me. I want to keep helping the team by giving it my all.” SEPTEMBER 10: Tasos Douvikas scores his team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Como 1907 and RB Leipzig at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Head coach Cesc Fabregas added: “From his very first day in Como, Tasos has demonstrated a strong mentality, and that has been reflected in his performances on the pitch. He is always positive, highly ambitious and has a fantastic work ethic. We are delighted to announce his contract extension.”

item.title: Burnley appoint Lopez as chief football officer
item.description: Diego Lopez has been recruited by Burnley from Genoa in Serie A [Getty Images] Burnley have appointed Diego Lopez as their new chief football officer with responsibility for football operations, recruitment and sporting structure. The 37-year-old Spaniard joins from Serie A side Genoa, where he held the same role and follows the club parting company with former manager Nicky Hayen following a damaging 4-1 defeat against Lincoln City on Saturday. Lopez, 37, joins with the Clarets in 22nd in the Championship after a dismal start to the season in which they have won just one game in 12. Club chairman Alan Pace told the club website Lopez's appointment was about raising standards across the football club. "We wanted someone with deep experience in recruitment and player development, a strong knowledge of European markets and a clear understanding of how those come together to strengthen a club over the long term," Pace said. "Diego has a proven record of exactly that." Hayen won the Belgian title with Club Brugge in 2024 and was brought in by Pace to oversee a promotion bid following Premier League relegation last season. Yet after a promising draw with West Ham on the opening weekend, their season has nosedived and the club are without a win at home in the league since beating Leeds United at Turf Moor in the Premier League over a year ago. Lopez has previously worked as a head scout at Monaco, Lille, Excelsior Mouscron and Bordeaux, while he also held a director of sport role at RC Lens. The appointment is understood to have been in the pipeline for some time given he left Genoa at the start of October. "I am eager to start exploring the great potential of this club," said Lopez. "I understand our mission and I believe in what Burnley can become in the coming years, if we all work in the same direction with full determination. "From my first conversations with Alan, it was clear there is real ambition here and a plan to match it." Latest Burnley news, analysis and fan views Ask about Burnley - what do you want to know?

item.title: 'It wasn't a farewell' - Michael Carrick breaks silence on Man Utd sack fears after Bournemouth humiliation
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-MAN UTD-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP Michael Carrick insists he has not said farewell to Manchester United despite a humiliating 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth raising serious questions about his future. The under-fire manager admitted he is completely in the dark regarding a potential dismissal as the club endures their worst start to a season in four decades. Worst start in forty years Carrick faces immense pressure after United suffered a demoralising 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth . The latest collapse means the club are currently enduring their worst start to a season in 40 years. The heavy home loss follows a crushing 4-1 thrashing by Como just days earlier. These consecutive dismal performances have left Carrick on the brink, with away supporters loudly taunting him during the latest defeat. Despite the hostile atmosphere from the travelling fans, Carrick received a warm reception from the United faithful as he headed down the tunnel. However, his long-term position remains highly uncertain. No farewells from the manager Despite the mounting scrutiny, Carrick completely dismissed the suggestion that he was waving goodbye to the supporters. He maintains that he is proceeding with his duties despite the widespread speculation. The manager confirmed he held a brief conversation with chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox following the final whistle. However, he remains entirely unsure if the hierarchy will ultimately dismiss him. "It wasn't a farewell from me," Carrick explained, as quoted by Independent . "Just briefly like always after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary. I will see what happens. I totally understand the situation. "I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I am carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything really. So that's kind of it. You know, I'm not expecting anything either way." Dressing room feeling the pain The dire run of form has taken a significant emotional toll on the playing squad. Carrick stressed that his team genuinely care about reversing their current negative trajectory. The manager also expressed his gratitude for the backing he received from the stands amid a turbulent period. "There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of disappointment, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, disappointed," he revealed. It's not like they don't care, or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to - I've not spoke to everyone individually, the ones I have spoken to, it's affecting them a lot." Carrick added: "Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way. To feel the connection and appreciation from the supporters, I feel it and appreciate it a lot." item.title: Preview: Part one of double-header
item.description: Preview: Part one of double-header Eintracht versus Hamburg, take one. We preview the DFB-Pokal tie that is the first of two meetings between the two clubs in the space of less than a week. Backdrop As the Bundesliga fixture list and DFB-Pokal draw would have it, Eintracht face Hamburger SV twice within a few days: in the second round of the cup on Tuesday 27 October at the Volksparkstadion, and then again five days later for Bundesliga Matchday 8 on Sunday 1 November at Deutsche Bank Park. Both teams lost 1-0 away in the league at the weekend, but came away from it with different feelings. Eintracht held Dortmund in check for much of the match and took plenty of positives and even a dose of self-confidence back to Frankfurt with them. There was discontent at Hamburg, however, after what was a “very frustrating day” and “not a good performance at all”, according to HSV’s Miro Muheim, speaking after their defeat to promoted side SC Paderborn. Despite the loss in Dortmund, Eintracht were very much looking on the bright side. “We put in a brave performance in the first half and we’re on the right track. I can see signs of progress,” said head coach Adi Hütter, with sporting director Timmo Hardung adding “we’re trending in the right direction”. Captain Robin Koch summarised: “We did well for long periods of the match. I can’t fault the team.” The sides are now set to face one another in the cup. “It’s knockout football and everyone’s going to be up for it,” said Elias Baum. “We’re away from home and we’re looking forward to it. We’ve proved that we can hurt any opponents and we’ll be taking that mindset into the match.” 1990 World Cup winner Uwe Bein, who played for both clubs during his career, commented: “I’m heading to Hamburg on 27 October. I was involved in plenty of cup ties up there and Eintracht always seemed to come out on top, so that might be a good omen.” “Make it through to the next round” The last time the teams met in the Bundesliga in May, Eintracht lost 2-1 at home, but they are unbeaten in seven trips to Hamburg in all competitions. And as Hardung put it: “We want to make it through to the next round on Tuesday.”

item.title: Jalen Williams is injured again, but OKC Thunder teammates know he'll 'fight back'
item.description: Loud City had never been more quiet. Fans shuffled out of Paycom Center in silence Sunday night as the usual victory anthem, Queen's "Don't Stop Me Now,” wasn't playing despite OKC's 108-101 win over the Los Angeles Clippers . It didn't feel right, given the tremendous loss the Thunder had just experienced. With 1:14 left in the contest, Jalen Williams went up for a dunk and was fouled by Kris Dunn . His left leg then folded underneath him when he landed, twisting his ankle to a 90-degree angle. OKC's players immediately called for the medical staff, and Williams was ultimately stretchered off the court. Some could be seen in tears. Others buried their face into a towel. And the uncomfortable silence continued in the locker room after the game, where the usual chatter didn't spill into the arena's tunnels. “Those are tough, man," Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault said. "We’re not doing great. That’s tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes, I think both teams, in those situations. We’re not doing great.” More: Jalen Williams stretched off court in Thunder vs Clippers game after gruesome leg injury Williams was upbeat just 24 hours prior to tipoff. He was in Stillwater, attending the Oklahoma State football team's 57-24 win over Colorado with his videographer and some close friends. He high-fived countless people in the crowd. He waived when placed on the Boone Pickens Stadium video board. And when asked by News 9 to record a message to Thunder fans, he shared his excitement for the new season. A clean slate after being limited to just 33 games last year due to a nagging, right-shooting wrist injury and multiple hamstring strains . "I'll be playing all year," Williams yelled into the camera. "Watch us live." Williams wasn't fully himself in terms of production during OKC's first two games of the season. Rust was to be expected, after all. But he was fully himself in terms of his personality. He raised the spirits, not just the play, of his teammates. He ran the floor with the enthusiasm of someone who'd been constrained to the bench. He took on tough matchups with the confidence of someone who'd conquered far bigger challenges. He celebrated every little win with the enthusiasm of someone who'd lost so much time. That palpable positivity is what made it so difficult to watch Williams get stretchered away Sunday night. It feels cruel that the guy who plays with the most joy is the one who has been kept off the court the most. And while Williams held both thumbs up in the air, determined to display some semblance of optimism, the look in his eyes didn't share the same sentiment. The tear streaks beneath them confirmed that. "I just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander quivered during a postgame sideline interview. "Nothing more than that." item.content:encoded: Loud City had never been more quiet. Fans shuffled out of Paycom Center in silence Sunday night as the usual victory anthem, Queen's "Don't Stop Me Now,” wasn't playing despite OKC's 108-101 win over the Los Angeles Clippers . It didn't feel right, given the tremendous loss the Thunder had just experienced. With 1:14 left in the contest, Jalen Williams went up for a dunk and was fouled by Kris Dunn . His left leg then folded underneath him when he landed, twisting his ankle to a 90-degree angle. OKC's players immediately called for the medical staff, and Williams was ultimately stretchered off the court. Some could be seen in tears. Others buried their face into a towel. And the uncomfortable silence continued in the locker room after the game, where the usual chatter didn't spill into the arena's tunnels. “Those are tough, man," Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault said. "We’re not doing great. That’s tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes, I think both teams, in those situations. We’re not doing great.” More: Jalen Williams stretched off court in Thunder vs Clippers game after gruesome leg injury Williams was upbeat just 24 hours prior to tipoff. He was in Stillwater, attending the Oklahoma State football team's 57-24 win over Colorado with his videographer and some close friends. He high-fived countless people in the crowd. He waived when placed on the Boone Pickens Stadium video board. And when asked by News 9 to record a message to Thunder fans, he shared his excitement for the new season. A clean slate after being limited to just 33 games last year due to a nagging, right-shooting wrist injury and multiple hamstring strains . "I'll be playing all year," Williams yelled into the camera. "Watch us live." Williams wasn't fully himself in terms of production during OKC's first two games of the season. Rust was to be expected, after all. But he was fully himself in terms of his personality. He raised the spirits, not just the play, of his teammates. He ran the floor with the enthusiasm of someone who'd been constrained to the bench. He took on tough matchups with the confidence of someone who'd conquered far bigger challenges. He celebrated every little win with the enthusiasm of someone who'd lost so much time. That palpable positivity is what made it so difficult to watch Williams get stretchered away Sunday night. It feels cruel that the guy who plays with the most joy is the one who has been kept off the court the most. And while Williams held both thumbs up in the air, determined to display some semblance of optimism, the look in his eyes didn't share the same sentiment. The tear streaks beneath them confirmed that. "I just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander quivered during a postgame sideline interview. "Nothing more than that." More: Jalen Williams injury deals an emotional blow to OKC Thunder. 'We’re not doing great' If there's any solace to be taken, it's that Williams won't feel bad for himself. He practices patience and perseverance in the face of adversity but not pity. It's how he played through a torn scapholunate ligament in his right shooting wrist during OKC's 2025 NBA championship run . And it's how he cleared the many hurdles thrown at him last season. “Dub is a resilient human being," Thunder guard Alex Caruso said. "He has great parents. He comes from a great family of hard work, love and putting your best foot forward at all times. The couple of years I’ve been here, getting to know his mom and dad, they raised their children right. Those characteristics and qualities are instilled in him as a person. "And, at a certain point, you can’t be a victim anymore. You have to take the adversity head-on, and you’ve got to fight back. He’s continued to do that, and I know he’ll continue to do it moving forward.” The only time Paycom Center came alive in the aftermath of Williams' injury was right before he was stretchered off the court. Chants of "J Dub" echoed throughout the arena from the 18,000 people in attendance. Then came an uproar of barks, a Thunder tradition Williams helped establish years ago. There was even a round of applause from the Clippers' players and fans as he disappeared into the tunnel. It didn't matter what team people supported. They were all in support of Williams. “No matter what, I think anybody in the arena can empathize with that," Daigneault said. "We appreciate our fans for doing so. We appreciate the Clippers for doing so.” An update on Williams has not yet been provided. Daigneault said the team will know more when it meets at its practice facility Monday morning. OKC must then host the Phoenix Suns later that night at 7 p.m. CT. It's a harsh reality of the basketball business. But the Thunder's players will handle it like the pros they are, just like Williams will handle the challenge ahead of him. And when he does make his return to Paycom Center, one thing is certain: The place won't be quiet. item.title: Against the odds, Grant Billmeier built NJIT basketball into a title contender
item.description: NEWARK – After a breakthrough third-place season in the America East Conference, NJIT basketball coach Grant Billmeier was not under the delusion that he would retain his nucleus. But he did set his sights on keeping talented freshman point guard David Bolden. “He’s someone a lot of guys want to play with, and the tampering for him was out of control,” Billmeier said. “It got to the point where he made an agreement to come back, he put it out there with (national reporter) Jeff Goodman, and I thought that would end everything. But it became, 'OK, now we know NJIT is the competition, how do we outbid them?’” Fortunately for Billmeier, the Milwaukee native was loyal to the lone Division 1 program that recruited him out of high school. “The kid didn’t want to go into a bidding war – this is where he wanted to be,” Billmeier said. “He’s a 4.0 student here and he’s the face of this program and he’s embracing that. In this day and age, when that doesn’t mean much, it means a lot to him.” Now, heading into the 2026-27 season, Bolden is preseason first-team All-America East as he majors in business and handles an academic courseload that includes calculus. “I love the school, I love the program, and they’ve been nothing but honest and open with me,” he said. “A lot of my peers, when they were freshmen, they didn’t get an opportunity to play like that. Looking at my opportunity here – I want to take advantage of that.” There’s a real opportunity for NJIT to make the NCAA Tournament for the first time. Bolden is surrounded by players: 6-foot-5 Georgia Tech transfer Brandon Stores, the cousin of assistant coach RaShawn Stores and the all-time leading scorer at St. Raymond High School in the Bronx; 6-9 returning forward and Rutgers Prep alum John Kelly; 6-10 Texas-San Antonio transfer Matheo Coffi; and 6-8, 237-pound freshman forward Victor Vanderstraeten, who played in Belgium’s top pro league. “There’s expectations now,” Billmeier said. “We’re very young – a lot of guys have to learn the system and how to defend – but the talent level is off the hook.” This is the fourth season at the helm for Billmeier, who is a former Seton Hall center and came up the coaching ranks as an assistant there. NJIT, with its academic rigor, presents some unique challenges: The only transfers in are incoming sophomores and postgrads. But he’s figured out how to balance the roster, and it helps to have connections. In this day and age, when that doesn’t mean much, it means a lot to him.” Now, heading into the 2026-27 season, Bolden is preseason first-team All-America East as he majors in business and handles an academic courseload that includes calculus. “I love the school, I love the program, and they’ve been nothing but honest and open with me,” he said. “A lot of my peers, when they were freshmen, they didn’t get an opportunity to play like that. Looking at my opportunity here – I want to take advantage of that.” There’s a real opportunity for NJIT to make the NCAA Tournament for the first time. Bolden is surrounded by players: 6-foot-5 Georgia Tech transfer Brandon Stores, the cousin of assistant coach RaShawn Stores and the all-time leading scorer at St. Raymond High School in the Bronx; 6-9 returning forward and Rutgers Prep alum John Kelly; 6-10 Texas-San Antonio transfer Matheo Coffi; and 6-8, 237-pound freshman forward Victor Vanderstraeten, who played in Belgium’s top pro league. “There’s expectations now,” Billmeier said. “We’re very young – a lot of guys have to learn the system and how to defend – but the talent level is off the hook.” This is the fourth season at the helm for Billmeier, who is a former Seton Hall center and came up the coaching ranks as an assistant there. NJIT, with its academic rigor, presents some unique challenges: The only transfers in are incoming sophomores and postgrads. But he’s figured out how to balance the roster, and it helps to have connections. During the offseason, when Billmeier was looking for a power forward, Christian Brothers Academy coach Brian Lynch recommended Vanderstraeten (Lynch is married to Belgian tennis great Kim Clijsters, and their daughter Jada played on a team with Vanderstraeten’s sister at one point). “Victor is probably further along right now than Patrik (Auda) and Sandro (Mamukelashvili) when they were freshmen,” Billmeier said, referring to two former Seton Hall standouts from Europe whom he coached. “He’s an exceptional passer.” Mamukelashvili became Big East Player of the Year and is now on a long-term NBA contract with the Los Angeles Lakers. “He makes all the right plays,” Bolden said of Vanderstraeten. “You can just tell he has a high IQ.” In a recent exhibition against American, which is the preseason favorite to win the Patriot League, Vanderstraeten posted 12 points and nine rebounds and Bolden chalked up 17 points, three assists, four steals and a whopping nine fouls drawn as the Highlanders prevailed 71-66. “We went through two tough years, but I think we’re in a good position in year four,” Billmeier said. item.title: Off-Script Ohio: Midseason awards, more chaos and the Heisman race
item.description: Ohio State was off this weekend, but college football didn’t slow down. Midseason Buckeye awards With the bye week giving us a chance to look back, Cole and Joey hand out their midseason awards. MVP, Offensive Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, Best Freshman, Best Transfer and Best Coach. Some picks are easy, and a couple of them lead to a real debate. Around college football Another week, another round of chaos. No. 2 BYU fell to UCF in double overtime, No. 8 Texas Tech lost at Cincinnati, Wisconsin blew out No. 16 USC (Ohio State’s next opponent), and Iowa and Tennessee both lost on walk-off field goals. Meanwhile, No. 6 Utah and No. 4 Indiana both survived. Heisman talk and the Big Ten race Jeremiah Smith is still the Heisman favorite at +120, but Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney are closing in and forming a clear top three. We also take a quick look at the Big Ten standings, where Ohio State and UCLA are both still unbeaten in conference play. CFP Top 10 To wrap up, Cole and Joey each give their College Football Playoff top 10. They agree on more than you’d think, but not on who belongs at No. 1.

item.title: Le Bris on Sunderland injury worry and Talbi’s situation after goalless draw with Leeds
item.description: Le Bris on Sunderland injury worry and Talbi’s situation after goalless draw with Leeds Régis Le Bris has played down concerns over Nordi Mukiele after Sunderland’s 0-0 draw with Leeds United. Asked about the defender’s condition after he was forced off, the Sunderland boss gave a brief but positive update. “He’s good now,” Le Bris said. Le Bris also addressed Chemsdine Talbi’s lack of game time and insisted the winger will get more opportunities, having been introduced as a late substitute on Sunday. “It started with the UEFA list,” he said. “It’s a shame because this list is so restrictive that you can’t use all your players. “It could have been really positive for him and for others as well to get minutes in this competition. “We started with two wingers, Nilson and Malick. “We trust them even if sometimes they are struggling. “I’m sure that Chemsdine will have these opportunities as well and it was a strong choice to give him an opportunity today, in a tight game, really intense, and I thought he could help. “It can be the case in the future.”

item.title: ‘We’ll see what happens’: Sophie Cunningham says there was ‘not a lot of warning’ on Fever changes
item.description: Jul 9, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) against the Phoenix Mercury at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The Indiana Fever are heading into a pivotal offseason with a very different front office. And it sounds like the changes caught some of the players by surprise. Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who is set to become a free agent, weighed in on the shakeup this weekend. She admitted that there “was not a lot of warning” before team president Kelly Krauskopf and general manager Amber Cox departed, but praised both as “phenomenal” people who cared about the players. Fever Shake Up Front Office The Fever’s season ended with a first-round playoff loss to the Las Vegas Aces, one year after the team reached the WNBA semifinals. On Friday, the team announced that Krauskopf would be stepping down after nearly three decades with Pacers Sports & Entertainment. Krauskopf helped build the franchise ahead of its inaugural season in 2000 and led the Fever to their first title in 2012. “She built it, delivered a championship and came back when we needed her,” team owner Herb Simon said in a statement . Hours later, the Fever fired general manager Amber Cox , according to The Athletic’s Annie Costabile . The team confirmed the move shortly after. Cox had joined the Fever in 2024 and oversaw roster construction. She also made headlines earlier this month when she said that “the attacks on our fan base have no basis in reality, and they need to stop,” via Awful Announcing . ‘Phenomenal People’ Speaking while at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, Cunningham was asked about the changes. “There was not a lot of warning and that’s OK,” Cunningham said in a clip shared on X . “I think that’s probably a good thing that you kind of keep it in-house a little bit.” She had nothing but good things to say about Krauskopf and Cox. “But you know what, Kelly and Amber, they’re phenomenal, phenomenal people,” Cunningham said. “They cared a lot about us as players and as individuals outside the court.” Cunningham also sounded a bit unsure about what comes next. “Hopefully the Fever come in and bring people who can do a really good job for that program,” she said. “I was blessed to be under Kelly and Amber and I hope them the very best. So, we’ll see what happens.” Cunningham is one of several key Fever players heading into free agency. She averaged 7.9 points per game this season while shooting 41.9% from three-point range, and she has become one of the most popular players on the team. Whoever takes over the front office will now have to decide whether to bring her back. The post ‘We’ll see what happens’: Sophie Cunningham says there was ‘not a lot of warning’ on Fever changes appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: How Adidas clapped back at LeBron James’ Anthony Edwards insult with a dig at Nike
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Adidas took the help of comedian Hasan Minhaj to get back at LeBron James and Nike. Over the years, Nike and Adidas have had a tug-of-war for the biggest basketball stars in the NBA, with most choosing the Swoosh brand over the Three Stripes. But in recent years, Adidas has slowly but surely grabbed some of the big names away from Nike, including Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards. Speaking of which, Edwards took a dig at LeBron James during the offseason in a commercial with Adidas. James clapped back by simply stating that he doesn’t watch anything from the Nike rival. Adidas and Hasan Minhaj get back at LeBron James and Nike James indirectly calling Adidas irrelevant has prompted a response from them, and they took the help of comedian Hasan Minhaj to get their point across. “Let’s focus on the face of the league, Ant Edwards. I’m talking about the highlights, the trash talk, the shoes. Look at these, they’re gorgeous,” Minhaj said. He added, “A certain someone in Philadelphia says he doesn’t watch the three stripes. Let me say this: your current company’s stock price says otherwise. I know you’re watching.” Ouch! That dig must sting the Swoosh brand, as the company’s stock price has plummeted since reaching record highs back in 2021. Adidas, on the other hand, has seen a sharp decline in its stock price as well, but the company is doing much better than Nike. Either way, after Adidas and Minhaj’s shot, Nike is likely working on the perfect clapback to make things even. item.title: Pat McAfee quickly reacts to Tom Brady’s ‘disdain’ over one NFL problem
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Pat McAfee was tuned in for Tom Brady’s commentary during the Green Bay Packers vs. Detroit Lions game, and appreciated one major comment he made. Brady’s role as an NFL commentator lends him a lot of authority, not just because of his incredible playing career, but also because of the role he plays in the NFL today. Since retiring, Brady has become part of the Las Vegas Raiders ownership group, a move that made his broadcast career a real problem at the beginning. Pat McAfee thanks Tom Brady for calling out unnecessary Roughing the Passer calls Taking to X , former NFL player-turned-analyst Pat McAfee reacted to Tom Brady expressing his frustration over the Roughing the Passer calls during the Green Bay Packers vs. Detroit Lions game. He noted that Brady was right to call out some of these decisions, and that as a respected player, lead announcer, and team owner, his views are held in very high regard. “I really appreciate Tom Brady’s disdain for some of these Roughing the Passer calls. He’s an owner and one of the lead commentators. He’s got A LOT OF WEIGHT.” Ironically, Roughing the Passer calls are something Brady had a problem with not being called enough during his playing career, and now he feels they’re being called too much. There were two Roughing the Passer calls during the Packers vs. Lions game, with Green Bay being called for both incidents. Brenton Cox Jr. in the third quarter and Karl Brooks in the fourth quarter were the recipients of the two big penalties, even though analysts like Brady were not in favour of such calls. In fact, even players on the field like Micah Parsons suggested that calls like these make the NFL feel like a flag football league. Officiating in the NFL has never been without scrutiny, but for a player with the cachet and authority of Tom Brady to point out an issue like this cannot be considered a good look. item.title: Spalletti admits Juventus performance was a tale of two halves
item.description: Spalletti admits Juventus performance was a tale of two halves Luciano Spalletti saw Juventus deliver an impressive first half against Lecce before their performance declined after the break. The Bianconeri secured a 2-0 victory , but the contrast between the two halves will give the manager plenty to consider as he looks to improve the team’s consistency. Juventus entered the match under considerable pressure following a difficult run of results. Reports suggested that Spalletti could face dismissal if his team failed to win against Lecce and Genoa , making the three points particularly important for his future at the club. The players were also under pressure to deliver stronger performances after struggling in recent weeks. They responded positively in the opening half, showing greater intensity, confidence and attacking intent as they took control of the contest. Spalletti praises Juventus’ first half The Juventus manager would have been pleased with the quality his players displayed before the interval. Weston McKennie opened the scoring in the 29th minute, while Douglas Luiz added a second in the 41st minute to give the visitors a comfortable advantage. Their performance reflected the kind of intensity and determination that supporters have been demanding. Juventus moved the ball effectively, created difficult situations for Lecce and looked capable of adding further goals during a dominant opening period. However, the second half presented a different picture. The Bianconeri became less convincing in possession, lost control of the game and allowed Lecce to grow in confidence. Their decline raised questions about their ability to maintain the same level throughout a match. Speaking via Calciomercato , Spalletti assessed both halves and explained why Juventus adopted a more cautious approach after the break. “Tonight they played a very serious first half, a high-level one, like a top-tier, tough team, a team that wanted to win the game. The satisfaction beyond the 2-0 is that we created difficult situations with a sequence like we did in the first half. Too many times we lacked the most precise pass that would have put us in a position to take the lead after our dominance in possession of the ball. In the second half, we dropped back, managed things a bit, lost a few timid balls, and they came back. But then it was 2-0, and the important thing was not to overextend ourselves and give them space.” (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Juventus must build on the result Spalletti acknowledged that his side became more passive after half-time, but emphasised the importance of protecting their two-goal advantage rather than giving Lecce opportunities to respond. The victory provides some relief amid the uncertainty surrounding his position. However, Juventus will need to produce more complete performances in their upcoming fixtures if they are to maintain momentum and ease the pressure on their manager.

item.title: Indiana football opens as 19.5-point favorite over Minnesota for Homecoming
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 24: Josh Hoover #10 and Joe Brunner #56 of the Indiana Hoosiers celebrate a touchdown during overtime of a college football game against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The Indiana Hoosiers won the game in overtime 13-6. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana football, sitting at 7-1 overall and 4-1 in the Big Ten, is set to welcome Minnesota on Saturday at Memorial Stadium in the Hoosiers’ homecoming matchup. The Hoosiers opened up as strong favorites in spite of some shaky play through most of the Big Ten slate up to this point. Indiana is a 19.5 favorite over Minnesota as of Sunday evening, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is set at 42.5 with marginally more favorable odds given to the under. Indiana is coming off of a road win against Michigan, the program’s first in Ann Arbor since 1967, while Minnesota is coming off of a home win over then-No. 15 Iowa. The Hoosiers are reeling some with quarterback Josh Hoover looking to return to full health while the Golden Gophers have had a bit of a weird stretch between aforementioned win over Iowa and a blowout loss at Purdue. On top of all of this, ESPN’s College Gameday will be in town, making the matchup just a bit bigger. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Improved notifications system! item.title: ‘It stinks’ – Kurt Warner offers sarcastic apology for mistaking Jaylen Warren for Colts player
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Kurt Warner offered an apology after he mistakenly referred to Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren as Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren on several occasions during the broadcast. This did not sit well with the Steelers nation, and they called out the former NFL quarterback for the mistake on X. However, Warner then engaged in a back-and-forth with several fans who were unforgiving about the error. The play came in the first quarter when Jaylen Warren rushed through the Saints’ defence to get the Steelers’ first down. He finished with 18 carries for 101 yards in a 16-10 Steelers win, which made things even worse for Warner. “We often think when you’re throwing a checkdown, it means a short play, but not when you’ve got Tyler Warren on the field. Get it to him, put the ball in the position he can catch and run and as we mentioned earlier. Nobody better in the league at the running back spot of yards-after-catch than Tyler Warren,” said Warner on-air. The clip of the play where Jaylen Warren is referred to as Tyler gained a lot of attention. Hours after the game, Warner accepted the mistake he made on-air. Kurt Warner apologises for referring to Pittsburgh Steelers RB as Tyler Warren Warner, who is a commentator for the NFL Network, had previously worked on the Indianapolis Colts’ game early in October. While explaining to fans, he stated that this proved to be a reason why he was confused. However, Warner accepted that the error was on his part. “Yes, I called JAYLEN Warren “Tyler” today after calling Colts game & referencing him in today’s game… My bad, so sorry… it stinks as an announcer when you do that & unfortunately it won’t be my last time bc sometimes u just react & misspeak! I own it… and JAYLEN was awesome today, so hopefully I gave him enough LOVE at other times!!” Warner wrote on X. He followed that up with a few responses to fans who were trolling him for the mistake. While Warner was accepting of any criticism, the former quarterback did not accept that he was unprepared for the coverage. “Seriously??? Did u listen to the game? I was more than prepared, just had Tyler on my mind bc I referenced him & just called his game… But a lousy mistake by me, but sometimes you misspeak, but unprepared is a weak call on your part!” Warner responded to a fan who stated that he was unprepared. Warner joined the NFL Network as an analyst in 2010. Since then, he has built a great reputation among fans with his analysis. While his mistake might have caused a stir among Steelers fans, Warner will continue to be an important part of the Network’s NFL coverage. item.title: MM 10.26: Maryland volleyball dismantled in straight-set loss to Michigan State
item.description: Maryland volleyball turned in one of its worst offensive showings just two days after its five-set collapse against Illinois. The Terps, who have the Big Ten’s second-worst attack, finished with a .147 hitting percentage and 18 attacking errors in a straight-set loss to Michigan State. Final Recap | https://t.co/ZMreHkrfbG pic.twitter.com/tUcX3pkN9J — Maryland Volleyball (@TerpsVolleyball) October 25, 2026 After producing a team-high 17 kills on Friday, Sydney Bryant only had four kills and a game-high eight attacking errors Sunday. Brooklynne Brass had 10 kills but needed 28 total attempts to do so. Trailing 4-3 early in the first set, the Spartans notched 12 consecutive points to open a double-digit lead. Maryland never had an answer, falling in the set, 25-13. Zora Hardison and Hayley Ogden sparked the run, combining for five kills and three blocks. While the Terps got off to a better start in the second set — they led 17-13 after a five-point run — Michigan State responded with seven unanswered points en route to a 25-23 set victory. The Spartans scored the final two points of the set. Maryland and Michigan State went back-and-forth in the third set, with neither team leading by more than three points. Despite hitting .269, four service errors haunted the Terps during their 25-23 set defeat. After exceeding last season’s Big Ten win total, Maryland has lost four straight matches — its won just two sets. In other news No. 20 Maryland women’s basketball avenged its NCAA Tournament second-round loss with a 72-68 exhibition victory over No. 12 North Carolina. Rachel Lawrence covered the game. No. 1 Maryland field hockey rebounded from its first loss of the season to beat No. 13 Indiana, 1-0, in a defensive affair. Roman Brunetti had the story. No. 11 Maryland men’s soccer recorded its second consecutive shutout during its 1-0 win over Ohio State. Rize Simmons had the coverage . Maryland volleyball blew a 2-1 lead, falling in five sets to Illinois and extended its four-game losing streak. Aarna Mishra provided the recap. Maryland women’s soccer produced just four shots in its 1-0 loss to No. 5 Michigan State. Noah Ghelli wrote the story. Maryland women’s golf is headed to the French Broad Collegiate Invitational. Teeing off in the French Broad Collegiate Invitational tomorrow! 🐢 👉 https://t.co/8Eu1KRgTcB pic.twitter.com/b352MQmShO — Maryland Women's Golf (@TerpsWGolf) October 25, 2026 Maryland wrestling completed its intrasquad scrimmage. We battled and got better tonight! Recap from 🔴⚫️: https://t.co/HDEBgphmfa #TurtlePower 🐢💪 #TFIN pic.twitter.com/G16K6Etdgf — Maryland Wrestling (@TerpsWrestling) October 25, 2026 Maryland baseball split its doubleheader against St. John’s Saturday. Dirty Terps hit the road today as the pitching staff racked up 27 strikeouts in 16 innings 🔥 #DirtyTerps pic.twitter.com/D7rxITrixF — Maryland Baseball (@TerpsBaseball) October 25, 2026 Maryland football is one of three power four teams without a win over another powe

item.title: Red Bull admits it cannot explain radio failures after Verstappen's sign language jibe
item.description: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has admitted the team is struggling to understand the persistent radio problems affecting Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar . Both drivers experienced communication failures during the United States Grand Prix, adding to the frustration within the Austrian outfit after similar issues disrupted the previous race weekend in Singapore. Red Bull unable to explain recurring radio failures Communication between the drivers and the pit wall proved problematic throughout the race in Austin, with Verstappen and Hadjar both experiencing difficulties receiving instructions from their engineers. The failures complicated Red Bull's efforts to manage the race, particularly at a time when strategy decisions were proving crucial. Speaking to media after the race, Mekies acknowledged that the team had yet to identify the cause of the recurring problems. The Frenchman also admitted that rival teams appeared to be handling radio communication more effectively. "If we were understanding it we would have solved it, so we don't fully understand why we are being hit by these issues. Certainly I have to admit that competition is doing a better job than us because we can obviously hear everyone's radio, and we have been struggling more than what we would have liked to." The issue has now affected Red Bull across consecutive race weekends, prompting the team to make finding a reliable solution a priority. However, Verstappen suggested that the problem has been occurring for considerably longer than the last two Grands Prix. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen jokes about using sign language after another radio failure The Dutchman made his frustration clear during the post-race press conference when asked about experiencing communication problems for a second time. Rather than accepting that description, Verstappen pointed out that similar failures had already occurred repeatedly throughout the season. "It's not the second time. It's already, I don't know how many times this year. Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It's probably cheaper as well. It's a disaster. Yeah, it's a disaster. It's really frustrating, to be honest." In Austin, Verstappen struggled to hear Tom Hart, who was working as his race engineer in place of Gianpiero Lambiase. The arrangement was intended to help the Dutchman and Hart develop their working relationship ahead of future races. The situation was different in Singapore, where Lambiase was unable to hear Verstappen's messages. The pair eventually resorted to coded communication to overcome the problem, but the measures taken by Red Bull since that weekend have failed to prevent further disruptions. Mekies previously indicated that the team wanted to introduce a more robust solution following the Singapore Grand Prix, although the difficulties experienced in Austin demonstrated that the issue remained unresolved. Mekies previously indicated that the team wanted to introduce a more robust solution following the Singapore Grand Prix, although the difficulties experienced in Austin demonstrated that the issue remained unresolved. Hadjar reveals how radio problems nearly caused costly mistake Verstappen was not the only Red Bull driver affected in Austin. Hadjar also struggled to communicate with his engineer, experiencing a problem he said was entirely new to him this season. "Honestly, for me it's the first time it's happening the whole year and I can tell you it's not nice," the Frenchman explained. "I can't hear anything." The lack of communication created confusion over when Hadjar was supposed to make his pit stop, with the Frenchman revealing that he nearly entered the pit lane at the wrong moment: "I don't know, I just hear some kind of box, box and then I box. I almost pitted at the wrong time once." His difficulties extended beyond the timing of his stop. Hadjar also revealed that he left the pit lane with the wrong engine map selected, while the decision to switch to hard tyres caught him by surprise. The communication issues added to an already complicated race for Red Bull, with Verstappen also expressing frustration over the team's strategy after finding himself stuck behind Hadjar, who was running a different pit-stop schedule. Red Bull faces another test at Mexican Grand Prix The upcoming Mexican Grand Prix could provide Red Bull with another opportunity to assess the problem, particularly as Verstappen's race engineer arrangements continue to change. Hart is scheduled to work with the four-time world champion in Austin, Brazil and Las Vegas, while Lambiase is expected to return to his usual duties in Mexico, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. The arrangements could also include Imola if other Grands Prix are cancelled. With both Red Bull drivers affected in Austin, the failures are not confined to Verstappen's side of the garage. Further problems with Lambiase back on the pit wall in Mexico could provide additional clues about whether the underlying cause lies in the car's communication equipment rather than the working relationship between driver and engineer.

item.title: Phillies Get Cancer Battle Update From 24-Year-Old Pitcher
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 25: A detail view of the Philadelphia Phillies logo atop the scoreboard at Citizens Bank Park during a game between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Philadelphia Phillies on September 25, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/IOS/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies face an important offseason after another disappointing playoff exit, with questions about their roster and coaching staff likely to shape the months ahead. The organization must determine how to strengthen a roster laden with highly paid and declining veterans as fans fear the championship window is closing. But not every meaningful development in the Phillies system involves baseball decisions. Amid the team’s offseason planning, an encouraging update has emerged involving a young pitcher whose year took a far more serious turn than anything that happens on the field. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cardinals Cut Ties With Hated Rival’s 4-Year Outfielder Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Pitcher Sends Cancer Surgery Message Gabriel Barbosa, a 24-year-old Phillies minor-league pitcher who was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer, has shared the results of a recent procedure. “I received the results of the surgery, and it was extremely positive!” Barbosa wrote in a translated caption on Instagram . “The test did not identify residual cancer in the surgical specimen, and the 128 lymph nodes analyzed were negative for carcinoma.” The results represent a very encouraging development for Barbosa, who recently welcomed his first child. His announcement follows a diagnosis that he shared during the summer, when the young pitcher began documenting his experience with the disease and its impact on his life. And it might have been aided by a recent charitable effort to raise funds for his battle. “There is a GoFundMe for Gabriel Barbosa, a Phillies minor leaguer who was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer and is expecting his first child with his wife this month,” The Athletic’s Matt Gelb shared last month . FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cubs’ 29-Year-Old Infielder Announces Retirement Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Receive Encouraging Update On Young Pitcher Barbosa’s announcement offered a welcomed moment of optimism for the Phillies organization and the fans who have followed his progress. Although the team has plenty of baseball matters to resolve before the 2027 season, his health update puts those concerns into perspective. “I also received news that, at this time, I will not need to do chemotherapy or radiotherapy,” Barbosa added in the caption. “There is the possibility of performing more immunotherapy for safety, but this will still be defined by the medical team.” For now, there is no telling when or if Barbosa might resume his journey toward the Phillies’ big-league roster. item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 10/26/26
item.description: Oct 13, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Taylor Walls (6) reacts after defeating the against the Cleveland Guardians in game two of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We got a breather after a breathless first two games of the World Series, with the two teams returning to action tonight as the series shifts to Florida. The Brewers only outscored the Rays by a total of two runs in Games 1 and 2, but they won both games, and the pressure is on Tampa Bay to turn this into a series back at home. They’ll have Freddy Peralta on the mound in service of that effort, with the righty coming off an ALCS MVP award and the team looking for him to continue what he’s done since he came over via trade from the Mets. It’ll be a light day on the site ahead of the Game 3 matchup, which will go off at 8 pm eastern and will see the Brewers counter with lefty Robert Gasser against Peralta. In the morning, you can catch Nick’s review of Tim Hill’s disappointing 2026 campaign, while Matt profiles Snuffy Sternweiss, not a household name as far as Yankees history goes, but the author of a couple of the greatest seasons we’ve ever seen from a lower-profile Yankee. Today’s Playoff Matchup: World Series Game 3 (Brewers lead 2-0) Tampa Bay Rays vs. Milwaukee Brewers (RHP Freddy Peralta vs. LHP Robert Gasser) Time: 8:00 p.m. EST TV: FOX/FOX One/Fox Deportes Venue: Tropicana Field, St. Petersburg, FL Questions/Prompts: 1. Who do you think has the pitching advantage tonight between the Brewers with Gasser and the Rays with Peralta? 2. As he’s set to become a free agent after the World Series, do you think Freddy Peralta has resuscitated his free-agent value with what he’s done down the stretch and in the playoffs?

item.title: Arteta expects Arsenal stars to have more belief in scoring from set pieces
item.description: Arteta expects Arsenal stars to have more belief in scoring from set pieces Arsenal scored from set pieces in their 2-0 victory over Everton at the weekend , giving Mikel Arteta reason to believe his side can become more dangerous from dead-ball situations. The Gunners found the net twice from set pieces, and their manager hopes the performance will help restore confidence in an area that attracted considerable attention last season. Arsenal were labelled ‘set-piece FC’ last term because of their frequent reliance on dead ball situations. Their effectiveness from corners and free kicks became a significant part of their campaign, while the club’s specialist set-piece coach, Nico Jover, also attracted attention and occasional mockery from rival supporters. Arsenal hope to rediscover their set piece threat Despite that reputation, Arsenal have relied less heavily on set pieces this season, finding goals through open play while continuing to collect results. Their reduced output from dead balls has meant the subject has attracted less discussion among rival fans, but the goals against Everton could mark a turning point. Arteta will hope the brace helps his players approach future set pieces with greater belief and conviction. The manager has consistently backed the work carried out on the training ground and believes the team’s preparation can translate into a greater threat during matches. Speaking to ESPN , Arteta said the goals could provide a psychological lift and strengthen the players’ trust in the approach. “I’m sure that’s going to unlock something and that belief of the players, so they are really convinced. “You have to see them when we train the level of attention and how much they believe in what we do and what Nico [Jover, set-piece coach] does as well. “There’s no question about that, but at the end he has to come through and he has to make the difference and we know that that is a massive welcome for us.” (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Arteta wants Arsenal to build on Everton win The manager’s comments underline the importance he places on the team’s set piece routines and the confidence required to execute them under pressure. Arsenal’s coaching staff have devoted considerable attention to this aspect of their play, and the Everton match offered a timely reward for that work. The Gunners will now aim to make the goals a starting point rather than an isolated success. If they can combine their threat from set pieces with their effectiveness in open play, they will have another route to breaking down opponents as the season continues. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Players left in ‘unusual’ position at latest PGA Tour event with no play on Sunday due to poor weather
item.description: Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images Many PGA Tour players, including Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler, know how challenging it can be to prepare for a playoff at an event when the additional holes are set to be played on a Monday. There is always an eerie atmosphere when a tournament bleeds into the start of a new week. Many will remember the bizarre feeling of Scheffler and Viktor Hovland’s playoff lasting less than 20 minutes at the Travelers Championship earlier this year, with the Norwegian emerging victorious. But there is an even stranger situation going on at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship right now, with Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power preparing for a Monday finish in Southampton. The two players will head to the 16th tee on Monday for their first shot in a tournament since Saturday due to the high winds in Bermuda. Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power reflect on unusual situation at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship It was decided that this year’s event would be cut down to 54 holes with the tournament organisers deeming that no play was going to be possible on Sunday. The problem was that Smotherman and Power are tied for the lead on 16 under par. With that, they will return for what many are presumably hoping will be a quick finale. Both men spoke about how bizarre the circumstances were after having to stick around on Sunday. “Yeah, I mean, it was such an unusual day kind of waiting to find out what exactly was going to happen. It’s a weird feeling, I’ve had a playoff before but obviously not overnight kind of thing. Looking forward to it. It’s going to be a different experience. Hopefully we’re able to get out there, most importantly,” Power said. “So yeah, it’s an unbelievable opportunity. Looking for win number three and you’ve got a one-on-one battle for it, so looking forward to getting out there and see what happens.” Smotherman said, when asked whether he had experienced anything similar: “I mean, no, absolutely not. Nothing like this remotely close. “I had one time at Q-School where I had a third round maybe rained out and we came back and played the next day. I think even Q-School a couple years ago in Jacksonville we had a whole third day off, played the next day kind of thing. So like not too unfamiliar with like rain delays, but being in a position we’re at, knowing we got up and down on 18 yesterday to make par to even have a chance. I know the tournament would probably prefer to have an outright leader right now, but we’ve still got work to do.” How important a victory could be in Seamus Power’s PGA Tour career A victory would be more significant for Power, as things stand. Smotherman, of course, recently won the Bank of Utah Championship on his 100th career start on the PGA Tour . He would actually move up just one place in the FedEx Cup standings with a win, going from 52nd to 51st. For Power, however, a win in Bermuda would move him from 103rd to 53rd. item.title: Havant & Waterlooville Women 1-3 Reading Women: Match Report
item.description: Mia Parker in possession, with Macey-Nikiah Walters watching on / | Alison Matthews Reading Women progressed to the second round of the League Cup with a 3-1 victory over Havant & Waterlooville at a blustery Westleigh Park on Sunday, producing a solid performance that was far more straightforward than in recent weeks. First-half goals from Sophie Bishop and Ellie Szekeres gave the Royals a comfortable 2-0 lead at the break. The hosts pulled one back through Sophie Lee shortly after half-time, briefly reducing the deficit, but Keren Banduka restored Reading’s two-goal advantage to secure the win and confirm a place in the next round. And all done in the presence of co-operating manager Rick Catania, who was very much part of the matchday action, on the touchline alongside the management and coaching team. As with their recent cup ties against Bromley in the FA Cup and Enfield Town in the Isthmian Cup, Reading were once again up against opponents enjoying an excellent run of form. Although the Hampshire side play a tier below Reading, in Division One South of the Southern Region Football League, they came into Sunday’s fixture sitting top of the table after taking maximum points from their opening four league matches. Havant & Waterlooville will be hoping to follow the well trodden path of clubs such as Farnham Town, Fleet Town and AFC Portchester, all of whom have recently secured promotion to the Premier Division. Their only defeat had come in the FA Cup, where they lost 3-1 to fellow Division One side AFC Stoneham. Like Reading, Havant & Waterlooville had also spent much of their early-season campaign on the road. Of their seven matches in all competitions, six had been played away from home, making Sunday’s encounter only their second appearance at Westleigh Park this season. Reading manager Ed Jackson-Norris reverted to a more familiar-looking starting XI, making six changes from the side that featured in mid-week. Scarlett Bowcott was handed her first appearance of the season in goal. Having featured throughout the Royals’ pre-season friendlies, the young and amiable shot-stopper made only her fourth senior start. Regulars Keziah Banduka, Ellie Luscombe, Bishop, Alice Curr and Nat Cowell all returned to the starting line-up. Mia Parker, Georgia Hayes, Ellie Manners, Keren Banduka and Macey-Nikiah Walters were named on the substitutes’ bench, but with no less of an important role still to play – Jackson-Norris often utilising his finishers to either see out a game or, as has been the case more recently, to claw themselves back into a match. Team (3-1-4-1-1): Scarlett Bowcott (GK), Bethan Poole (Alice Curr, 89’), Keziah Banduka, Lara Moore, Poppy Whitburn (Georgia Hayes, 70’), Ellie Szekeres (Mia Parker, 55’), Ellie Luscombe, Freya Morgan, Alice Curr (Ellie Manners, 76’), Nat Cowell (captain) (Keren Banduka, 70’) Sophie Bishop (Macey-Nikiah Walters, 70’) Reading goalscorers: Sophie Bishop, 7’; Ellie Szekeres, 20’; Keren Banduka, 72’ Havant & Wa
item.content:encoded: Mia Parker in possession, with Macey-Nikiah Walters watching on / | Alison Matthews Reading Women progressed to the second round of the League Cup with a 3-1 victory over Havant & Waterlooville at a blustery Westleigh Park on Sunday, producing a solid performance that was far more straightforward than in recent weeks. First-half goals from Sophie Bishop and Ellie Szekeres gave the Royals a comfortable 2-0 lead at the break. The hosts pulled one back through Sophie Lee shortly after half-time, briefly reducing the deficit, but Keren Banduka restored Reading’s two-goal advantage to secure the win and confirm a place in the next round. And all done in the presence of co-operating manager Rick Catania, who was very much part of the matchday action, on the touchline alongside the management and coaching team. As with their recent cup ties against Bromley in the FA Cup and Enfield Town in the Isthmian Cup, Reading were once again up against opponents enjoying an excellent run of form. Although the Hampshire side play a tier below Reading, in Division One South of the Southern Region Football League, they came into Sunday’s fixture sitting top of the table after taking maximum points from their opening four league matches. Havant & Waterlooville will be hoping to follow the well trodden path of clubs such as Farnham Town, Fleet Town and AFC Portchester, all of whom have recently secured promotion to the Premier Division. Their only defeat had come in the FA Cup, where they lost 3-1 to fellow Division One side AFC Stoneham. Like Reading, Havant & Waterlooville had also spent much of their early-season campaign on the road. Of their seven matches in all competitions, six had been played away from home, making Sunday’s encounter only their second appearance at Westleigh Park this season. Reading manager Ed Jackson-Norris reverted to a more familiar-looking starting XI, making six changes from the side that featured in mid-week. Scarlett Bowcott was handed her first appearance of the season in goal. Having featured throughout the Royals’ pre-season friendlies, the young and amiable shot-stopper made only her fourth senior start. Regulars Keziah Banduka, Ellie Luscombe, Bishop, Alice Curr and Nat Cowell all returned to the starting line-up. Mia Parker, Georgia Hayes, Ellie Manners, Keren Banduka and Macey-Nikiah Walters were named on the substitutes’ bench, but with no less of an important role still to play – Jackson-Norris often utilising his finishers to either see out a game or, as has been the case more recently, to claw themselves back into a match. Team (3-1-4-1-1): Scarlett Bowcott (GK), Bethan Poole (Alice Curr, 89’), Keziah Banduka, Lara Moore, Poppy Whitburn (Georgia Hayes, 70’), Ellie Szekeres (Mia Parker, 55’), Ellie Luscombe, Freya Morgan, Alice Curr (Ellie Manners, 76’), Nat Cowell (captain) (Keren Banduka, 70’) Sophie Bishop (Macey-Nikiah Walters, 70’) Reading goalscorers: Sophie Bishop, 7’; Ellie Szekeres, 20’; Keren Banduka, 72’ Havant & Waterlooville goalscorer: Sophie Lee, 48’ Reading yellow cards: Ed Jackson-Norris, 74’ Havant & Waterlooville yellow cards: Mille McNamara, 76’ First half In an assured start from the kick-off, it was the Royals who struck first. From a Reading throw-in, Cowell’s early pressing helped force the ball into the path of Morgan on the right wing. Demonstrating great confidence, she took on her defender and delivered a dangerous ball into the box. Bishop collected it and showed excellent composure to control, take a step and stroke the ball past goalkeeper Sara Luce for a smart finish and an early lead for the Royals. 0-1 . There were rapturous cheers of delight and relief from the travelling fans. This was the first time in five matches that Reading had taken the lead, dating back to the end of September, when Szekeres opened the scoring against Oxford City at the SCL Stadium. Reading doubled their lead in the 20th minute from their first corner. Curr’s delivery was only partially cleared, with the ball falling to Szekeres on the edge of the penalty area. She controlled it well before unleashing a shot into the bottom corner, putting the Royals firmly in control. 0-2 . Jackson-Norris’s game plan is built around playing through midfield, and on Sunday, the central trio demonstrated just how effective this can be. Luscombe provided a strong, protective base, while Szekeres intercepted play and moved possession forward with purpose. Combined with Morgan’s vision and quality of passing, the trio tirelessly worked together to unlock defences and create opportunities for the Reading front line. The pace of Bishop and Curr, combined with Cowell’s strength leading the line, meant the Royals looked dangerous with every attack. Reading came close to extending their lead on several occasions throughout the first half, with their movement and running causing the Hawks defence plenty of problems. Morgan and Bishop combined once more, the midfielder’s weighted through ball being played into the path of the Reading striker. Bishop’s effort was bravely blocked by Hawks goalkeeper Luce, whose excellent save denied the Royals another goal. Curr went close soon after, latching onto a dangerous cross whipped in by right-wing-back Whitburn. Her effort was fired narrowly wide of the back post as Reading continued to press and put the match beyond reach. At the other end, Reading goalkeeper Bowcott had relatively little to do during the first half. However, with the hosts always a threat from counter-attacks, she needed to remain alert. With just five minutes of the half remaining, she demonstrated this to perfection, racing off her line at just the right moment to bravely clear the danger as Havant & Waterlooville’s number nine, Lauren Aitken, bore down on goal – her quick reaction ensuring Reading kept their two-goal advantage at the break. Half-time: 0-2 After a first half in which Reading had looked firmly in control, they switched off early in the second, making life for themselves (and the Loyal Royals) just a little harder than it needed to be by conceding only three minutes after the restart. The home side were given far too much time and space down their right, allowing Ruby Saunders to deliver a cross into the box for Lee to tap home unchallenged from close range. 1-2 . Just minutes later, the hosts came controversially close to equalising, with the Hawks’ top goalscorer Millie Bradbury firing narrowly wide. The opportunity came amid strong appeals from the Reading players, after defender Keziah Banduka had been clearly wrestled to the ground in the build-up, only for the referee to wave play on. The referee’s leniency and growing inconsistency in the officiating contributed to what became a feisty and fiery end to the match. Poole, Moore, Keziah Banduka and Parker all found themselves on the receiving end of some heavy challenges but showed great restraint. Jackson-Norris was shown a yellow card, following his protests over a foul on Reading captain Cowell, who had entered the game as a substitute. The Hawks’ Millie McNamara was also cautioned for one of the more innocuous infringements during the second half. The introduction of Walters, Keren Banduka and Hayes with 20 minutes of normal time remaining highlighted both Reading’s character and the strength in depth available from the bench. As on Wednesday, albeit in very different circumstances (with Reading trailing 4-0 midweek), Jackson-Norris reshaped his side, reverting to a flat back four. The versatile Hayes was moved into central defence to help shore up the back line and ensure the Royals could see the game out. However, it was the attacking impact of Walters and Keren Banduka that paid almost immediate dividends, with the pair combining just two minutes after their introduction to restore Reading’s two-goal advantage. A long ball from Keziah Banduka sent Curr chasing to poke the ball beyond the onrushing goalkeeper, but stumbled

item.title: ‘Not the Strongest Indication of Actual Interest’ — Packers Reporter Stops Hype Train in Its Tracks as Rumors Link Green Bay With $44 Million All-Pro RB
item.description: ‘Not the Strongest Indication of Actual Interest’ — Packers Reporter Stops Hype Train in Its Tracks as Rumors Link Green Bay With $44 Million All-Pro RB With the Nov. 10 trade deadline two weeks away, the rumor mill is running at full speed, and it just put the Green Bay Packers’ name next to Jonathan Taylor’s. Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter’s Sunday report for ESPN on the Indianapolis Colts’ deadline options listed the Packers with the Seattle Seahawks, Minnesota Vikings, and Denver Broncos among the teams tied to a possible trade for the star running back. Hours later, the Colts fell to 2-5 with a 16-10 loss in Minnesota. According to the report, that was the first of three games that will help decide whether Indianapolis has a fire sale in two weeks. However, how much to read into Green Bay’s spot on that list depends on who’s doing the reading. Packers Reporter Pumps The Brakes on Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors After the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard, rival teams began watching film and weighing ways to acquire Taylor, guard Quenton Nelson, and defensive tackles DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, according to the report. People briefed on the Colts’ approach believe the team wants to try to win its next three games before the deadline. Should that fail, Ed Dodds, the new chief of personnel who long served under Ballard, will join owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon in moving pieces to build for the future. The first leg of that plan went sideways on Sunday. Taylor did his part with 18 carries for 95 yards, including a 38-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, and Indianapolis led 10-6 at halftime. Then the Vikings, one of the four teams named in the report, scored the game’s final 10 points to improve to 6-0. Zach Kruse, managing editor of The Packers Wire, chose to zero in on the wording. He shared the report’s line, which he credited to Schefter and Rapoport, describing the four clubs as teams that “have pondered, or are expected to consider,” a trade. Then he dropped a one-line verdict: “Not the strongest indication of actual interest.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Why Others Still See the Packers in the Mix Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson, weighing in on who could trade for Taylor before Sunday’s kickoffs, started from Indianapolis’ side of the table: “I’m not trading him because he’s my best player and I need this guy for the long-term.” Even so, he offered a different read on Green Bay: “To me, the interesting team here (is) if I’m the Green Bay Packers. The first leg of that plan went sideways on Sunday. Taylor did his part with 18 carries for 95 yards, including a 38-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, and Indianapolis led 10-6 at halftime. Then the Vikings, one of the four teams named in the report, scored the game’s final 10 points to improve to 6-0. Zach Kruse, managing editor of The Packers Wire, chose to zero in on the wording. He shared the report’s line, which he credited to Schefter and Rapoport, describing the four clubs as teams that “have pondered, or are expected to consider,” a trade.
